item.title: Loss of Monotonicity in the Vector Play Model and Consequences for Newton-Type Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2611.00168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The vector play model (VPM) replaces the implicit minimization of the energy-based hysteresis model (EBM) by an explicit update. Its tangent contains the product of the Hessians of two unrelated potentials and is unsymmetric. Hence, the VPM has no co-energy density at frozen memory, and the skew part makes $\boldsymbol{H}\mapsto\boldsymbol{B}$ lose monotonicity in a band just outside the pinning circle, into which small time steps drive the sliding states. In composite models, the determinant of the tangent can change sign, which explains published failures of the local inversion $\boldsymbol{B}\mapsto\boldsymbol{H}$, and where it is negative, $\boldsymbol{H}\mapsto\boldsymbol{B}$ is not injective. In the scalar potential formulation, the exact tangent keeps a descent guarantee, whereas symmetric surrogates of the tangent, such as the symmetrized tangent or Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) updates, lose it and become ascent directions where the skew part dominates, as computations of TEAM Problem 32 confirm. It is therefore recommended to use solvers with an unsymmetric tangent.
item.dc:creator: Dominik Cibicki, Klaus Roppert, Manfred Kaltenbacher

item.title: A Hierarchical direct solver for Lippmann-Schwinger equations based on boundary traces
item.description: arXiv:2611.00494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A high-order hierarchical direct solver for variable-media scattering in two dimensions is presented. Standard discretizations for these problems produce dense linear systems that are commonly solved iteratively, requiring a new global solve for each incident field. The method proposed here instead constructs a reusable scattering operator for the inhomogeneous medium, based on a hierarchical subdivision of the computational domain. First, high-accuracy leaf scattering operators are built from discretized local integral equations. Up the hierarchy, neighboring boxes are merged to build the scattering operators for successively larger boxes. A key feature of the method is that each scattering operator is represented as a map of incoming traces to outgoing traces. Consequently, volume unknowns appear only in the leaf computations; all higher levels of the hierarchy operate entirely on boundary traces. The hierarchical solver is presented first at the continuum level and discretized only afterward using high-order local volume quadrature, polynomial trace representations, and boundary integral techniques. For a discretization involving $N$ degrees of freedom, the method requires $O(N^{3/2})$ work and $O(N\log N)$ storage to build all scattering operators. Once these are available, any incoming field can be processed at cost $O(N)$ if only the outgoing field is required, and cost $O(N\log N)$ if the full field is required. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy on a range of challenging scattering problems including cavities, back-scattering, limited regularity, and high wavenumber, that pose significant challenges to iterative methods.
item.dc:creator: Yunhui Cai, Simon Dirckx, Joar Bagge, Per-Gunnar Martinsson

item.title: A comparison of parallel iterative methods for ILU triangular solves
item.description: arXiv:2611.00552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exact triangular solves parallelise poorly, limited by the size and number of the level sets, so on GPUs the factors from incomplete LU (ILU) factorisations are often solved approximately with parallel iterative methods. We compare four such methods: a Jacobi method, an Incomplete Sparse Approximate Inverse (ISAI), GMRES polynomials, and AIRG, a reduction multigrid built on GMRES polynomials, for which we introduce a parallel coarse/fine splitting that bounds the diagonal dominance ratio of the fine-fine block. We test them with ILU(0) and ILU(1) factors of canonical PDE problems and 91 SuiteSparse/Matrix Market matrices, the latter on a single GPU. AIRG is the most robust on the PDE factors, with nearly flat iteration counts under refinement and no per-problem tuning, but has the largest setup and memory costs. GMRES polynomials are more robust than the Jacobi method at a similar cost. As the inner solve of an ILU preconditioner with tuned inner iteration counts, ISAI gives the largest median speedups over a hipSPARSE exact triangular solve (4.5$\times$ and 6.8$\times$ for ILU(0) and ILU(1)), though this was dominated by smaller problems; on the largest ILU(1) problems all four methods give similar median speedups of 2.1-2.6$\times$.
item.dc:creator: S. Dargaville, C. C. Pain

item.title: Unconditional optimal convergence of a relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for 2D space-fractional NLS
item.description: arXiv:2611.00571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a linearly implicit relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for the two-dimensional space-fractional nonlinear Schr\"odinger (SFNS) equation, where the fractional Laplacian is approximated by a simple fractional central difference scheme. The proposed scheme is uniquely solvable and conserves discrete mass for general real-valued nonlinear coefficients, and a modified discrete energy in the cubic case. By introducing a modified error system employing a cut-off technique, we establish the optimal-order error estimates without mesh-ratio restriction. Specifically, the primary variable achieves second-order temporal and spatial convergence in the discrete $H_h^{\alpha/2}$-norm, and the relaxation variable satisfies the same convergence in the discrete $L^2$-norm. Some numerical experiments confirm the relevant theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Lisen Ding, Dongling Wang

item.title: Parameter Bounds and Inverse Approximation for Linearized ReLU$^k$ Networks on the Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.00656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study direct and inverse approximation for linearized shallow ReLU$^k$ networks on $\mathbb S^d$ with quasi-uniform hidden parameters. For $0<\alpha<\frac{d+2k+1}{2d}$, under the coefficient growth condition $\bigl(n\sum_{j=1}^na_{j,n}^2\bigr)^{\frac{1}{2}}\leq n^\alpha M$, we prove that approximation at the order $n^{-\frac{d+2k+1}{2d}+\alpha}$ is equivalent to membership in the parity-compatible Besov space $\mathcal B_{2,\infty,*}^{\frac{d+2k+1}{2}-\alpha d}(\mathbb S^d)$. Mere convergence under the same coefficient budget does not imply this regularity. For unconstrained approximation along a nested parameter sequence, a single ridge function gives a counterexample when $\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$, whereas for $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ the endpoint Besov inverse conclusion follows from a Bernstein inequality under antipodal quasi-uniformity. The inverse conclusion is also recovered when the prescribed rate holds for two quasi-uniform parameter sequences whose union is antipodally separated.
item.dc:creator: Yuqing Liu, Tong Mao, Jonathan W. Siegel, Jinchao Xu

item.title: A posteriori error estimates for a finite volume approximation of a local sensing Keller-Segel model
item.description: arXiv:2611.00767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A local sensing Keller-Segel model, in which cells adjust their motility to the local chemoattractant rather than its gradient, and a semi-implicit finite volume scheme for its numerical approximation are studied. Computable a posteriori bounds for the approximation error measured in terms of the $L^\infty(0, T; H^{-1}(\Omega))$ and $L^2(0, T; L^2(\Omega))$ norms of the cell density are derived based on a new stability estimate and suitable reconstructions of the flux and the flux potential of the numerical solution. Optimal scaling of the estimates is numerically demonstrated in 1D and 2D experiments. Moreover, an adaptive mesh refinement method steered by the estimator is proposed for the 1D case, and its efficiency is numerically verified.
item.dc:creator: Niklas Kolbe, Kiwoong Kwon

item.title: Flux vector splittings and semi-implicit finite volume schemes for an isentropic two-phase flow model
item.description: arXiv:2611.00781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present two new semi-implicit finite volume schemes for the 1D hyperbolic and thermodynamically compatible (HTC) isentropic two-phase flow model of Romenski et al., written in terms of mixture density, volume fraction, partial gas density, mixture momentum and the relative phase velocity. In gas-liquid mixtures, the sound speed of the weakly compressible liquid is much larger than the gas sound speed and flow velocity, so the time step of fully explicit discretizations is dictated by liquid acoustic waves, even when the interest lies in the dynamics of the gas. To overcome this difficulty, the model's flux is split at the continuous level into an explicit subsystem (gas dynamics) and an implicit subsystem (liquid acoustic waves), leading to a nonlinear system for liquid pressure solved with the Newton method. In the first splitting the entire liquid phase is treated implicitly, while in the second the liquid convective terms are moved to the explicit subsystem, so only liquid acoustic waves are treated implicitly and nested Picard iterations are avoided. Thus, the time step of both schemes is restricted only by flow velocities and gas sound speed, independent of liquid sound speed. We prove and numerically confirm that both schemes exactly preserve the Abgrall condition (uniform velocity and pressure across material interfaces). For well-prepared initial data, both schemes are consistent with the volume balance of the liquid's low Mach number limit. Riemann problems, pressure equilibrium tests and acoustic tests show that in non-stiff regimes the semi-implicit schemes reproduce the results of a fully explicit scheme, while in the stiff regime they allow time steps that are up to 3-4 orders of magnitude larger, avoiding the excessive numerical dissipation of explicit schemes whose numerical viscosity is dictated by liquid sound speed.
item.dc:creator: Michael Dumbser, Gabriella Puppo, Alessandra Spilimbergo, Tommaso Tenna

item.title: A Second-Order Stochastic Dynamic Mode Decomposition by Richardson Extrapolation
item.description: arXiv:2611.00793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic dynamic mode decomposition (SDMD) approximates the Koopman semigroup of an It\^o diffusion by a Galerkin generator matrix on a dictionary of observables, computed from samples of the invariant law and evaluations of the generator, and advances observables with a first-order stochastic Taylor step (SDMD-1). The second-order Taylor step (SDMD-2) also needs the matrix of second generator actions, hence a dictionary with four derivatives, evaluations of a fourth-order differential operator at every sample, and a third matrix. We show that the Richardson extrapolation of two SDMD-1 half steps (SDMD-R) is second-order accurate with the data, the matrices, and the regularity of SDMD-1. One error bound covers exact and empirical Galerkin matrices. It consists of the Galerkin error of the dictionary, which is common to all schemes, a time-stepping term, and a data term of order $m^{-1/2}$ in the sample size $m$. The time-stepping term is $O(\dt^2)$ for SDMD-R and $O(\Theta_N\dt+\dt^2)$ for SDMD-2, where $\Theta_N$ is the norm of the second-order Galerkin residual $\Proj_N\cA(I-\Proj_N)\cA|_{\cV_N}$. The first-order term is attained and, for self-adjoint generators, vanishes only for generator-invariant dictionaries. For reversible periodic diffusions and trigonometric dictionaries with cutoff $K$, the step restriction $\dt\lesssim K^{-2}$ makes all three schemes contractions, and the error against the Koopman semigroup on $H^\ell$ observables is $O(K^{-(\ell-2)}+\dt^p)$ plus a sampling term of order $K^{d+2}m^{-1/2}$ in dimension $d$, with $p=1$ for SDMD-1 and $p=2$ for SDMD-R and SDMD-2. Numerical experiments confirm that SDMD-R matches or improves on the accuracy of SDMD-2 at the cost of SDMD-1.
item.dc:creator: Yuanchao Xu

item.title: Efficient second-order physics-preserving schemes for incompressible flows with variable density and viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2611.00834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a novel second-order prediction--filter--projection framework for incompressible flows with variable density and viscosity. In this framework, a constrained $L^2$-projection is enforced to unconditionally preserve the prescribed density bounds and discrete mass conservation, while a generalized-Laplacian reformulation combined with the D-CSAV approach is used to discretize the variable-viscosity momentum equation. In particular, a density-weighted second-order time filter is proposed, which eliminates the additional uniform-in-time bound restriction imposed on the time difference quotient of the discrete density in existing stability analyses. The resulting scheme is shown to satisfy an unconditional modified-energy dissipation law, without the viscosity-related restrictions imposed in earlier work. Then, an additional scalar auxiliary variable and its compatible temporal discretization are introduced to construct a variable-step prediction--filter--projection scheme. This scheme is also bound-preserving and mass-conserving, and satisfies an unconditional modified-energy dissipation law. Moreover, the modified energy is much closer to the ``original'' kinetic energy, differing from it only through the auxiliary-variable corrections. Based on the variable-step scheme, a reliable energy-based adaptive time-stepping strategy is developed. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, physics-preserving properties, and efficiency of the proposed schemes.
item.dc:creator: Baolin Kuang, Lanxin Sun, Rihui Lan, Hongfei Fu

item.title: A structure-preserving finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility
item.description: arXiv:2611.00837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct and analyze a fully discrete finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility. The scheme combines a standard two-point flux approximation of diffusion, the L1 approximation of the Caputo derivative on a uniform time grid, and a semiconvex splitting of the potential, and it discretizes the inverse mobility by a secant average multiplying the entire L1 derivative. The key estimate is a lower bound for the accumulated pairing of this weighted L1 derivative with the solution increments in terms of the accumulated L1 quadratic form. Using this lower bound, we derive a discrete energy estimate and the time regularity required for compactness. For twice continuously differentiable semiconvex potentials satisfying sign conditions outside $(-1,1)$ and initial data in $H^1(\Omega)$ taking values in $[-1,1]$, we prove existence of at least one fully discrete solution on every admissible finite volume mesh and every uniform time grid. Every such solution satisfies the maximum bound principle and a discrete energy bound relative to the initial energy, without a time-step restriction. In up to three space dimensions, under a mesh regularity condition with a constant independent of the mesh size, we prove that any sequence of fully discrete solutions has a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2(\Omega\times(0,T))$ to a weak solution of the continuous problem as the mesh size and time step tend to zero. As a consequence, we obtain existence of a weak solution in one and two space dimensions, and in three dimensions whenever such meshes exist.
item.dc:creator: Yonghyeon Jeon, Kiwoong Kwon

item.title: A Clustered Equivalent-Source Method with Local Response Compression and Group-Symmetry Reduction for Antenna-Array Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.00914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-wave analysis of finite antenna arrays is computationally demanding because detailed element responses must be resolved and coupled across the entire array. To reduce this cost, this paper presents a clustered equivalent-source method that combines local response compression with group-symmetry reduction. Local responses are represented in compressed equivalent-surface bases or coordinates inherited from child clusters. Symmetry constraints associated with the cluster partition and excitation reduce the coupled system, while the corresponding group transformations recover the complete response in the retained coordinates. To assess overall efficiency, we evaluate the costs of local construction, propagation, global solution, and recovery. Numerical examples involving layered and finite annular patch arrays show close agreement between the computed and reference complex far fields and shorter complete-run times than those of the corresponding symmetry-reduced direct solvers. Among the three equivalent-source implementations for the layered array, the one with the smallest coupled system has the longest runtime because local construction and propagation dominate the cost. These findings highlight the need to consider local construction and coupling costs when assessing the benefit of reducing the global system dimension.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Zhao, Liang Li, Xing Li, Hao Kang

item.title: Alternative Tikhonov-Type Regularization for the Calder\'on Inverse Conductivity Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.01034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the application of two regularization methods, classical Tikhonov and Alternative Tikhonov regularization, to the Calder\'on inverse conductivity problem. We develop an iterative reconstruction scheme based on linearizing the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and approximating conductivity updates using Gaussian basis functions. The resulting linear systems are solved using both regularization methods, with particular attention given to the derivation and numerical implementation of Alternative Tikhonov regularization. We compare the performance of these methods through numerical experiments on a synthetic conductivity containing two localized regions of differing conductivity. A total of 666 reconstruction tests are performed across varying regularization parameters, damping factors, and iteration counts. The lowest relative reconstruction errors obtained are 0.064730 for Alternative Tikhonov and 0.065173 for classical Tikhonov regularization. Although both methods produce comparable reconstructions, Alternative Tikhonov achieves the lowest observed error. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of both approaches within the proposed reconstruction scheme and motivate further investigation into parameter selection, numerical stability, and reconstruction accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Pavel B. Dubovski, Charles Morehead

item.title: Massively parallel Schwarz methods for the high-frequency Helmholtz equation with O(k) convergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.01075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a one-level restricted additive Schwarz solver with perfectly matched layer transmission conditions (RAS--PML) for high-frequency Helmholtz systems. For problems with ${O}(k^d)$ unknowns, $d=2,3$, the solver uses Cartesian decompositions and ${O}(k^d)$ concurrent local solves for a single right-hand side, where $k$ is the wavenumber. Starting from the convergence theory for fixed decompositions established in~\texttt{arXiv:2404.02156}, we address the growing cost {as $k$ increases} of local solves through a nested RAS--PML construction. Under suitable stability and contraction assumptions, we prove that sufficiently accurate recursive local solves preserve convergence of the outer iteration. We also prove that a single inner iteration at each non-terminal level yields a correction algebraically equivalent to one-level RAS--PML, provided that the hierarchy-induced finest local problems and composite restriction and weighted extension operators are retained. This equivalence provides a hierarchical interpretation and permits a direct implementation without recursive transfers. We assess the one-level solver using PML and overlap widths of order ${O}(k^{-1}\log k)$. Constant-coefficient experiments cover $300\leq k\leq19200$ in two dimensions and $60\leq k\leq780$ in three dimensions, reaching $1.47\times10^9$ and $4.75\times10^8$ complex unknowns, respectively. Richardson iteration counts grow approximately linearly with $k$ over these ranges, while total parallel runtime, including setup and solution, exhibits near-linear growth at the larger tested wavenumbers. Further experiments assess the effects of mesh refinement and heterogeneous media.
item.dc:creator: Yan Xie, Yue Yu, Shihua Gong, Ivan G. Graham, Chen-song Zhang

item.title: Minimum-Norm Interpolation in Weighted Variation Spaces: Direct and Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study minimum-norm interpolation in weighted variation spaces generated by ReLU$^s$ ridge functions on the unit ball, where $s$ is a positive integer. For a target $f$ in the weighted variation space and a node set with sufficiently small fill distance $h$, every minimum-norm interpolant satisfies the direct bound $\|f-\mathscr{I}_{X_h}f\|_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}h^{(2s+1)/4}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$. Under a boundary separation condition on the nodes, we construct a matching lower bound for the worst-case interpolation error. For the inverse problem, we introduce dual certificates and derive an estimate analogous to a Bernstein inequality. Under suitable upper bounds on dictionary size and spectral lower bounds for the atomic Gram matrices, sufficiently fast $L_2$ convergence of minimum-norm interpolants along geometrically decreasing fill distances implies that the target belongs to $\mathcal{V}_s$. As a byproduct, the best $L_2$ approximation error $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}$ for shallow ReLU$^s$ networks of width at most $n$ satisfies $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}n^{-1/2-(2s+1)/(2d)}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, with the weighted atomic cost of an approximating network bounded by a constant multiple of $\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, independently of $n$.
item.dc:creator: Weizhao Li, Lei Shi, Hanfei Zhou

item.title: An Incidence-Based Edge-Averaged Method for Convection-Diffusion Problems on Polytopal Meshes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an incidence-based edge-averaged method for scalar convection-diffusion problems on convex polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimensions. The proposed method extends the classical edge-averaged finite-element scheme through a graph-theoretic formulation based on vertex-edge incidence matrices. We first establish this formulation on simplices in arbitrary dimensions and then extend it to convex polytopes by introducing complementary edges and generalized barycentric coordinates. A key ingredient is a matrix identity that relates the generalized Whitney edge mass matrix to a diagonal representation of the Poisson stiffness matrix, enabling an exponentially-fitted discretization expressed entirely in terms of nodal values and edge weights. We prove that the resulting stiffness matrix is a nonsingular $M$-matrix under suitable positivity and connectivity conditions, ensuring monotonicity and the discrete maximum principle. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional simplicial and nonsimplicial meshes demonstrate first-order convergence in the $H^1$ semi-norm and stable, nonoscillatory solutions in convection-dominated regimes.
item.dc:creator: James H. Adler, Xiaozhe Hu, Seulip Lee, Eoghan O'Keefe

item.title: Online Autotuning of Algebraic Multigrid via Contextual Bandits and Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.01193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are widely used for solving large sparse linear systems, but their efficiency depends strongly on interacting setup and solve parameters. Effective parameter choices typically depend on the problem. We develop a phase-aware online autotuning method for hypre's BoomerAMG to reduce cumulative time-to-solution over sequences of related linear systems. A LinUCB-based contextual bandit selects mixed-type parameters for AMG hierarchy construction using a shared cost model over PDE descriptors and configuration encodings. A recursive LSTDQ controller uses residual and timing observations to estimate the AMG solve time within each attempt and adapt relaxation weights between multigrid cycles. Both learners update from ongoing solves without offline pretraining. Across grids of sizes $40^3$, $60^3$, and $80^3$, the joint autotuning method reduces total runtime, including recurring learner computation, by 36.1-43.3% for diffusion problems and 19.8-31.0% for diffusion-advection problems over sequences of 5000 linear systems, relative to the reference BoomerAMG default configuration. On a variable-flow diffusion-advection benchmark comprising 30,000 systems on a $60^3$ grid, 2 systems fail to converge with joint autotuning, compared with 1677 for the reference configuration, under their respective attempt budgets.
item.dc:creator: Xudong He, Ruiyu Wang, Yilang Ding, Rui Peng Li, Yuanzhe Xi

item.title: Fully Discrete Error Analysis of the CSLDG Scheme with Numerical Characteristic Tracing and Spline Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.01448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element scheme based on the characteristic Galerkin method (CSLDG) is investigated.The scheme directly discretizes an integral invariant model derived from the coupling of the transport equation and its adjoint equation.we have established, for the first time, error estimates for the fully discrete CSLDG scheme over a general domain \Omega in \mathbb{R}^d.The error is decomposed into three parts: the ideal numerical solution error (the difference between the exact solution and the spatial discretization), the time-dependent test function error (the deviation of the test function caused by the numerical characteristic backtracking via an ODE solver), and the upstream region approximation error (the integration region deviation induced by numerical characteristic backtracking and spline boundary reconstruction).Under either compact-support boundary conditions or periodic boundary conditions with the velocity field and the solution sharing the same spatial periodicity, without requiring incompressibility,and assuming the standard CFL condition (\Delta t=O(h)) linking the time step and the mesh size, the following results are proved:Using piecewise P^K polynomial spaces, the L^2 error of the ideal numerical solution attains a suboptimal order O(h^K); If the ODE solver order satisfies D \ge 2K+2+d, the overall error retains the suboptimal order even after incorporating the time-dependent test function error;When the upstream region approximation error is further taken into account, for d \ge 2 the overall error remains suboptimal O(h^K) provided the spline reconstruction degree satisfies r \ge \max(K+1+d, d+2);
item.dc:creator: Zhengrong Xie

item.title: Robust preconditioners for finite element approximations of control-state constrained optimal control problems governed by elliptic equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this paper is to derive robust preconditioners for integral control-state constrained optimal control problems governed by the second order partial differential equations with linear finite element approximations. We give corresponding discretized systems of the first order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions, and get six linear algebraic systems with saddle point schemes. Furthermore, we propose efficient block preconditioners to solve the corresponding linearized algebraic systems. With respect to both mesh sizes and inherent parameters, the robustness of proposed preconditioners is proved with explicit eigenvalues of minimal polynomials. Meanwhile, we design two algorithms and choose the incomplete $LU$ factorizations to deduce the computations. Two numerical experiments are given to depict the efficiency of our proposed preconditioners.
item.dc:creator: Juan Zhang, Liang Ge, Jianwei Zhou

item.title: Rank-Optimal Sample Complexity of Riemannian Gauss-Newton for Low-Rank Matrix Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2611.01542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the recovery of an unknown rank-$r$ matrix $\boldsymbol{X}_\star \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n_2}$ from Gaussian linear measurements using the Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN) algorithm. Each iteration of RGN solves the RGN equation followed by a fixed-rank retraction. We prove that, with high probability, RGN with spectral initialization converges quadratically to $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$ using $\mathcal{O} ( r(n_1+n_2)\kappa^2 )$ measurements, where $\kappa$ is the condition number of $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$. This is the first result to simultaneously achieve rank-optimal sample complexity and quadratic convergence for Gaussian low-rank matrix sensing. The key to the proof is a sharp spectral-norm analysis of the iterates, which requires controlling the inverse operator arising from the RGN equation. Our analysis develops an exact finite Neumann expansion of this inverse operator and combines it with a virtual-sequence decoupling argument and the restricted isometry property. Extensive numerical experiments support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the advantages of RGN.
item.dc:creator: Xunmeng Wu, Jian-Feng Cai, Zongben Xu, Zai Yang

item.title: Energy-Dissipative, High-Order BDF Schemes for Simulating Geometric Flows via Energy Increments
item.description: arXiv:2611.01593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose energy-dissipative backward differentiation formula (BDF) methods for geometric flows in the Barrett--Garcke--N\"urnberg (BGN) parametric finite element framework. Starting from a Lagrange-multiplier formulation, we replace the multistep approximation of the energy derivative by an energy-increment equation while retaining the BDF geometric equations. The Simpson quadrature and two interleaved time grids provide third- and fourth-order constructions. The positive quadrature weights ensure stepwise decay of the original discrete geometric energy for every nondegenerate solution of the nonlinear system. We establish an explicit conditional consistency bound for the scalar energy equation and a regularity criterion for the Newton system of curve-shortening flows. Then, the proposed schemes extend to simulating curve diffusion, mean curvature flow, and surface diffusion. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate geometric accuracy, energy decay, good mesh distribution, and high performance of the proposed schemes.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqing Pan, Wei Jiang, Jiwei Jia

item.title: Parameter-robust preconditioners for a stabilized control-volume discretization of Biot's equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze parameter-robust block preconditioners for a stabilized control-volume discretization of the quasi-static Biot equations. Beginning with a five-field formulation, we eliminate the poroelastic stress and time-scaled Darcy velocity through independent vertex-local solves, obtaining a symmetric cell-centered displacement--rotation--pressure system. A macrocell rotation-jump term stabilizes the weak-symmetry constraint. We prove the well-posedness of the fully discrete scheme and show that the condensed, coupled displacement--rotation mechanics block is uniformly spectrally equivalent to its block-diagonal counterpart. For uncoupled preconditioners, we derive an exact discrete pressure-control criterion and a sufficient parameter condition that accommodates the scaling \(c_0\asymp K_{\rm dr}^{-1}\), thereby allowing the storage coefficient to vanish in the nearly incompressible limit. We then construct a Schur-consistent pressure block that approximates the mechanics-induced pressure correction and prove its uniform equivalence to the exact pressure Schur complement. These results yield parameter-independent spectral bounds for block-diagonal preconditioning and weighted field-of-values estimates for lower-triangular preconditioning. Practical realizations employ a macrocell mass-matrix approximation for the stabilized rotation block and tailored two-grid solvers for the displacement and pressure blocks. Numerical experiments verify the expected convergence behavior in two dimensions and demonstrate robust performance under mesh refinement and broad variations of the physical parameters in both two and three dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Lei Wei, Lina Zhao

item.title: The Ehrlich--Aberth root finder is not generally convergent
item.description: arXiv:2611.02143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the well-known Ehrlich--Aberth root finding method is not generally convergent. More precisely, we show that there is an open subset of polynomials of any degree $d\ge 7$, and an open subset of initial conditions, such that the iteration of the Ehrlich--Aberth method converges to an attracting periodic cycle of period $4$, rather than to a vector of roots. The proof is constructive in the sense that we present explicit values for the polynomial and the $4$-cycle. The search is highly non-trivial: we found no attracting cycles for lower degrees/periods, and the size of the attracting domain relative to a ``unit cube'' in the space of polynomials and starting vectors is on the order of $10^{-127}$.
item.dc:creator: Torben Grabbel, Nedim Srkalovic, Dierk Schleicher

item.title: Unconditionally $L^2$-stable explicit--implicit--null filtered Runge--Kutta methods for general nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.02282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop unconditionally $L^2$-stable explicit--implicit--null (EIN) filtered Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with space-, time-, state-, and gradient-dependent diffusion coefficients. The methods are linearly implicit in the sense that they evaluate nonlinear terms explicitly and require only linear solves. Unlike classical EIN methods that are direct applications of implicit--explicit (IMEX) RKs, our construction is built upon explicit RKs. The key ingredient is two-sided symmetric filtering applied at each RK stage: a high-order filter is applied both before and after evaluating the original nonlinear residual. It leads to a dissipation estimate independent of the time step and retains the underlying RK order formally. Assuming time-dependent splitting operators with stagewise pointwise coefficient bounds, we rigorously prove non-increasing $L^2$ norm for arbitrary time steps. A quadratic matrix criterion covers explicit RK-based methods with positive weights, while strong stability preserving (SSP) compositions yield exact energy identities and weighted dissipation estimates. We present SSP methods through fourth order and a method based on the classical RK4. The framework accommodates spatial discretizations with discrete gradient structures including continuous Galerkin, Bassi--Rebay 1, the method of Brezzi et al., and local discontinuous Galerkin. Compatible summation-by-parts discretizations with simultaneous approximation terms are also covered in their discrete mass norm.
item.dc:creator: Yue Wu, Chi-Wang Shu

item.title: Embedding a de Rham Complex Structure into Eig-PIELM for Maxwell Eigenvalue Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary condition alone does not eliminate the gradient nullspace of the Maxwell curl-curl operator. Consequently, a boundary-only Maxwell implementation of Eig-PIELM, an eigenvalue extension of the physics-informed extreme learning machine (PIELM), may retain represented gradient modes in its reduced trial space, producing nonphysical, gradient-contaminated modes. We develop dR-Eig-PIELM, a finite-dimensional structure-preserving extension that retains the linear-coefficient, boundary-null-space, and one-shot multimode architecture of Eig-PIELM. It combines compatible tensor-product grad--curl trial spaces with a constrained null-space construction to restrict the sampled PEC space to the mass-orthogonal complement of the represented gradient image before the eigensolve. Symmetric weak-form Gram assembly yields a symmetric-definite reduced eigenproblem without an eigenvalue cutoff under the stated sampling and material-positivity assumptions. For rectangles and cuboids, we establish fixed-degree exactness at the PEC vector-field space and derive rank and dimension identities. Numerical experiments show that dR-Eig-PIELM excludes the spurious eigenmodes with significant gradient components observed in the boundary-only baseline. The method exhibits rapid convergence with increasing polynomial degree and competitive work--precision performance in the tested configurations. A covariantly mapped waveguide example illustrates the potential of dR-Eig-PIELM for integration into design optimization workflows through a constrained local geometry update driven by computed cutoff frequencies and their sensitivities. This work provides a mathematical and computational framework for separating represented gradient modes from physical Maxwell eigenmodes within Eig-PIELM and supports its use in waveguide spectral analysis and geometry design.
item.dc:creator: Hao Kang, Liang Li, Xing Li

item.title: Alias Geometry and Density Compensation in Perturbed Fourier Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.02379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a uniform grid with equal weights, Fourier modes that remain distinct on the grid are exactly orthogonal. When the nodes are perturbed, density compensation readjusts the weights. We ask how much of the resulting error reweighting can remove, measuring it by the Frobenius norm of the Gram defect, whose square is proportional to the mean-square error of density-compensated adjoint reconstruction. The answer is governed by aliasing. The grid cannot distinguish certain frequency differences, so a weight correction must treat each such alias class as a single number, while a node displacement affects every frequency difference in the class separately. To first order, reweighting removes the class average but not the spread. The irreducible error is a sum of covariance matrices, one for each class of colliding frequency differences. If no differences collide, every small node perturbation can be repaired exactly with positive weights. With collisions, a repair that works to first order can fail at second order. At the two-dimensional DFT, row and column shears are each exactly repairable, but their combination is not, and we compute the obstruction. In one dimension, oversampling protects a band of low-frequency node motions, and under random jitter optimal reweighting asymptotically removes a fraction $1-\kappa^2(2-\kappa)^2$ of the expected squared first-order error at oversampling ratio $\kappa\in[1,2]$. At critical sampling, node and weight perturbations are orthogonal: no reweighting helps, Voronoi weights can never reduce the error, and for the one-dimensional DFT the remaining error is a log-Vandermonde energy with the circular $H^{1/2}$ energy as its continuum limit.
item.dc:creator: Erli Wind-Andersen

item.title: High-Order Unconditionally Stable IMEX BDF--FEM Schemes for the Hodgkin--Huxley Model on a Branched Axon
item.description: arXiv:2611.02423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct and analyze high-order implicit--explicit backward differentiation formula finite element (IMEX BDF--FEM) schemes for the Hodgkin--Huxley cable system on a branched metric graph. The linearly implicit schemes combine constant-step BDF methods of orders $q=1,\ldots,5$ with conforming finite elements of any fixed degree $p\ge1$. Extrapolated gate variables are smoothly masked before evaluating the conductances, preserving coercivity without projecting the numerical gates. A voltage cutoff makes the gate rates globally bounded and Lipschitz. Each timestep requires one linear voltage solve followed by independent nodal gate updates. Under exact spatial integration, we prove unconditional stability of the complete fully discrete regularized scheme in discrete history energies. Under regularity and starting-history assumptions, the voltage and reconstructed gates converge in $L^2(\Gamma)$ at the optimal rate $O(h^{p+1}+\Delta t^q)$, without a timestep restriction or an $h$--$\Delta t$ coupling. The same rate holds with numerical quadrature when its full residual defect is $O(h^{p+1})$. Manufactured solutions recover the predicted orders through BDF5--$P_4$. Action-potential simulations illustrate pulse propagation and splitting, while a controlled work--precision comparison within the proposed family shows that higher-order variants can reach a prescribed accuracy at much lower runtime along the tested joint-refinement paths.
item.dc:creator: Hayden Reed, Qingguang Guan

item.title: Two-point residual step size gradient methods for linear systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kaczmarz-type methods often converge slowly when the coefficient matrix is ill-conditioned. In particular, when the smallest singular value is small, every row of the coefficient matrix is nearly orthogonal to the corresponding right singular direction, so that the iteration stalls along that direction. To break this slow-convergence regime, we borrow the delayed-step-size idea of the Barzilai-Borwein (BB) method and, within the framework of the residual-based surrogate-hyperplane Kaczmarz method, propose two new step sizes for gradient-descent-type methods solving linear systems: a delayed residual step size \(\alpha_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\) and a residual-difference step size \(\alpha_k^{\mathrm{RD}}\), which correspond, respectively, to the BB1 and BB2 step sizes in convex quadratic optimization. We prove that \(\alpha_k^{\mathrm{RD}}\le\alpha_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\), and we analyze the convergence of the resulting method in a canonical model with two singular values: although the step sizes are non-monotone, the residual norm is shown to decrease after finitely many steps. Numerical experiments on some ill-conditioned linear systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Xin Xu

item.title: POD-CNF: reduced order modeling of parametrized stochastic PDEs via normalizing flows and proper orthogonal decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.02787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reduced-order models (ROMs) learned from trusted numerical simulations enable the real-time simulation of complex physical systems, making computationally prohibitive tasks-such as uncertainty quantification and optimal control-tractable. In particular, data-driven ROMs are opening the opportunity to learn from both numerical simulations and experimental data. However, integrating these sources of information is far from straightforward. Real-world measurements often involve multiple sources of uncertainty, including non-Gaussian noise, latent heterogeneities, unknown or hidden system parameters, and multiscale phenomena occurring below the resolution of the data. Consequently, real-world data are better described by parametrized stochastic partial differential equations, for which the development of effective ROMs remains relatively unexplored. In this work, we introduce POD-CNF, a data-driven generative ROM for efficient uncertainty quantification of parametrized high-dimensional systems. The approach combines projection-based model reduction and deep generative modeling. First, Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is employed to obtain a low-dimensional representation of the solution manifold. A Conditional Normalizing Flow (CNF) is then trained to approximate the density of the reduced coefficients conditionally on the input parameters. This formulation allows the surrogate to capture complex, multimodal output distributions, going beyond standard regression-based ROMs and least-squares predictions. We assess the effectiveness of POD-CNF through numerical experiments, demonstrating its ability to accurately reproduce output distributions while substantially reducing computational costs. Finally, a proof-of-concept application illustrates how the generative paradigm facilitates integration into Bayesian inverse problems, highlighting promising directions for future research.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Violante, Nicola Rares Franco, Andrea Manzoni

item.title: A Legendre-Based Modified Extreme Learning Machine for Convection-Diffusion Equations: Steady-State, Continuous-Time, and Discrete-Time Formulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.02800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convection-diffusion equations are fundamental models for transport phenomena, but their numerical solution becomes challenging in convection-dominated regimes due to steep gradients and sharp boundary layers. This motivates the development of accurate approaches capable of effectively resolving such features while avoiding costly iterative optimization. In this study, a modified ELM framework based on shifted Legendre polynomials is developed for convection-diffusion equations in steady-state, continuous-time, and discrete-time formulations. The proposed approach is evaluated on steady and unsteady benchmark problems with relatively high Peclet numbers, including continuous and discontinuous boundary conditions. Finite element method solutions are used as independent solution references. By exploiting the linearity of the governing equations, MELM determines the output weights through a single least-squares solve, avoiding the iterative gradient-based training required by PINNs. The shifted Legendre polynomial basis provides an effective spectral representation for resolving steep gradients and sharp boundary layers. For the DT-MELM formulation, the coefficient matrix remains unchanged across successive time levels, allowing its LU or QR factorization to be computed once and reused. A systematic comparison with PINNs that incorporate advanced training strategies demonstrates that MELM provides higher accuracy and shorter solution times for steady-state and DT-MELM formulations across the benchmark problems considered. In contrast, CT-MELM exhibits scalability limitations as the size of the space--time basis increases. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of MELM for steady-state and discrete-time convection--diffusion problems, while also showing that PINNs provide better scalability for large space--time formulations where global CT-MELM becomes computationally demanding.
item.dc:creator: Gadade Navnath Ankush, Ram Shiromani, Tomas Gandara, Ramon Codina, Sivaram Ambikasaran

item.title: Compressed Multiscale Kernel Collocation and Physics-Informed Kernel Learning for Elliptic BVPs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kernel collocation is a meshfree method for partial differential equations whose accuracy depends on the smoothness of the kernel and of the solution. For globally supported kernels, however, the collocation matrices are dense and severely ill-conditioned. We address both issues by combining a multiscale collocation scheme with samplets, a multiresolution basis of discrete signed measures with vanishing moments. In the samplet basis, the collocation matrix has only O(N log N) relevant entries, while the multiscale scheme adapts the kernel width to the spacing of the points on every level. Since the differential operator scales the equations at the interior points differently from those at the boundary points, the rescaling alone does not bound the condition number of the level systems. We therefore solve them by a Schur-complement reduction that is invariant under this scaling. For noisy data, we consider physics-informed kernel learning, which replaces the collocation system by a regularized least-squares fit. We show that it reduces to collocation as the regularization vanishes, and we solve it by a deflated conjugate gradient method that reuses the Schur-complement reduction. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, with exact and noisy boundary data, show that the method handles significantly more points than dense collocation.
item.dc:creator: Sara Avesani, Manel Babay, Angela Kunoth, Michael Multerer

item.title: Optimal L^2 Error Estimates for CSLDG Ideal Numerical Solutions in Time-Dependent Compressible Periodic Flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.02867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the characteristic Galerkin-type semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element (CSLDG) method for conservative linear transport equations. When the characteristic maps and upstream regions are exact, each update of the ideal CSLDG scheme is equivalent to exact conservative transport of the current numerical solution followed by L^2 projection onto the background DG space. The conventional estimate obtained by accumulating projection errors over successive time steps loses one order when \Delta t\asymp h, but this loss does not represent the actual accuracy of the scheme. For smooth velocity fields \A(\x,t) on a common periodic lattice, we construct local correctors used only in the analysis on uniform Cartesian meshes, assuming that \Delta t/h is fixed and that every component of the local Courant vector remains uniformly separated from the integers throughout the space-time domain. We prove strict contraction of the reference-cell transport-projection operator on the zero-mean polynomial space, establish uniform solvability of the corrector equation and Lipschitz estimates with respect to its parameter, and control the difference between the exact flow map and a local frozen translation through weak integral moments. This yields a one-step residual of order O(h^{K+2}), and, while retaining the step-by-step update and the standard L^2-projected initial data, gives, for the P^K approximation, an optimal O(h^{K+1}) error bound. The velocity may depend on both space and time, and incompressibility is not required. An appendix extends the analysis to a compact-support setting, in which the velocity field and the solution need not share a common spatial period.
item.dc:creator: Zhengrong Xie

item.title: Efficient Numerical Evaluation of Arbitrary High-order Partial Derivatives via Algebraic Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.02948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing high-order partial derivatives of multivariate functions is often computationally and memory intensive. This paper addresses this problem via an algebraic approach. High-order partial derivatives of a multivariate function are expressed as linear combinations of univariate directional derivatives, which are computationally friendly. The coefficients and direction vectors are determined by the Waring decomposition of monomials, so that the number of univariate directional derivatives in the representation is minimized. Numerical experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Shuixin Fang, Hang Zeng

item.title: Information Limits for Stable Reduction of Coupled Diffusion Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Eliminating an unresolved diffusion field from a coupled parabolic system produces an operator-valued memory term and a contribution from the hidden initial state. We study whether a reduced prediction of the retained field meets a prescribed tolerance. For known hidden initial data, the discarded response, damped by diffusion and transmitted through the coupling, gives an upper error bound; an auxiliary diffusion problem supplies a lower bound. Rigorous discretisation bounds then yield tests that accept, reject or remain undecided. If the discarded initial state is known only through a norm bound, the minimum worst-case error equals that bound multiplied by the time-uniform gain from the missing state to the retained trajectory. Our main result encloses this infinite-dimensional gain using a finite spectral Galerkin evolution, its residual in the full equations and an explicit diffusion tail. The enclosure converges without compactness or smallness of the coupling. Strict comparisons of the optimal radius with a tolerance have finite certificates if all endpoint quantities admit arbitrarily accurate rigorous enclosures. Multiplication-coupling examples with infinitely many dynamically coupled modes illustrate both settings, including explicit finite-element error budgets.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Ishizaka

item.title: Computational performance versus numerical accuracy in the acoustic terms of weakly-compressible SPH
item.description: arXiv:2611.02994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate computation of the acoustic terms in weakly-compressible SPH, including the equation of state, its inverse, and the evaluation of the local speed of sound, is essential to ensure energy conservation, robust solid boundary conditions, and correct open boundary behavior. In the classic Cole's equation of state, using values of the polytropic constant $\gamma \ne 1$ can lead to significant precision loss, particularly when computations are performed in single precision, as is common in GPU implementations. We extend here our previous results on the optimal choice of state variable by introducing a new higher-precision form for all three acoustic terms, denoted \texttt{explog}, and assess its numerical accuracy and computational performance across a variety of devices and test cases. We find that the new form evaluates the acoustic terms with a maximum ULP of~2 for arguments less than $0.125$, and has higher errors in less than 1\% of the arguments larger than the threshold. Combined with a rewritten expression of the pressure at solid boundary particles in the ``dummy'' model, it provides consistently more accurate results, maintaining deviations from the reference pressure profile to below 2\%, even in presence of a rough bottom terrain. Computationally, the new formulation is also faster than the naive one on GPU, and only marginally slower on CPU.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Bilotta, Alireza Zarei, Roberta Cristofaro, Alexis H\'erault, \'Elie Saikali, Morteza Derakhti

item.title: Adaptive accuracy-driven splitting in Ozaki matrix multiplication and application to block LU factorization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Ozaki scheme for matrix multiplication computes an accurate matrix product by splitting the input matrices and evaluating a sequence of low-precision matrix products. Its accuracy and computational cost depend strongly on the number of splits. We develop accuracy-driven criteria for selecting this number in both Ozaki matrix multiplication and in block LU factorization using Ozaki trailing updates. For matrix multiplication, we derive normwise and componentwise criteria that determine how many split products are required to achieve a given accuracy requirement. For block LU, we present a fixed normwise strategy with essentially no selection cost, an LU-aware adaptive normwise strategy that can reduce the number of splits in subsequent trailing updates, and a componentwise strategy that uses information accumulated from preceding updates to guide the later selections. In the componentwise strategy, when the required number of splits exceeds a prescribed maximum, the corresponding update is instead carried out using ordinary matrix multiplication. We also provide rigorous backward error bounds for these approaches. Numerical experiments show that the adaptive normwise strategy can reduce the number of splits while preserving normwise accuracy, whereas the componentwise strategy can provide smaller componentwise backward errors when stronger local accuracy is needed.
item.dc:creator: Erin Carson, Yuxin Ma

item.title: Multi-GPU Acceleration of Interface Problems in FEniCS, with Application to Cardiac Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.03181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GPU acceleration of finite element assembly is well established for standard formulations, but mixed-dimensional problems, in which volumetric subdomains are coupled via lower-dimensional interfaces, remain unsupported in automated frameworks such as FEniCS. We extend cuDOLFINx, a GPU-enabled extension of the DOLFINx finite element framework, to assemble such interface problems on GPUs while preserving the high-level FEniCS programming model. Combined with GPU-resident Krylov solvers and algebraic multigrid preconditioning, this enables end-to-end GPU execution of the EMI (Extracellular--Membrane--Intracellular) model, an elliptic interface problem from cardiac modeling in which many intracellular subdomains are coupled through membranes. We compare the GPU implementation against a CPU-based one through strong and weak scaling experiments on regular and realistic 3D cardiac geometries with up to 8000 cells and 22 million degrees of freedom. In terms of assembly, a single GH200 node is roughly equivalent to two 144-core CPU nodes in strong scaling, and to two to three nodes in weak scaling, depending on geometry. For the linear solver, performance depends on geometry, preconditioning, and problem scale. On the regular geometry, GPU advantages emerge mainly at larger problem sizes and node counts. On the realistic geometry, with the same algebraic multigrid preconditioner for both architectures, the GPU is faster at all tested scales. The implementation is available as open-source software and applies to other problems with interface coupling.
item.dc:creator: Edoardo Centofanti, Benjamin Pachev, Joshua Steyer, James D. Trotter, Pietro Benedusi

item.title: Kernelized Stable Fluids for simulating physically accurate solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Stable Fluids algorithm is a fractional step method for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in an unconditionally stable way. It was initially developed for visual effects and allows real-time simulations because of its low computational complexity. The method solves the advection step by using the method of characteristics which is implemented via linear interpolation. This results in excessive diffusion of vorticity and is one of the main reasons for the physical inaccuracy of the algorithm. We propose Kernelized Stable Fluids with Sparse Cholesky Preconditioning (KSF-Chol) in order to address this shortcoming and make the algorithm thereby suitable for engineering problems and scientific computing. The algorithm is modified by replacing the linear interpolation approach with kernel interpolation in the advection step. We accelerate the computationally expensive kernel interpolation by using sparse Cholesky preconditioning and a near-/far-field approach and optimize both methods for computations on a uniform Cartesian grid. KSF-Chol achieves per time step a near-linear computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N\log^d(N/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{chol}}))$ in space and time. We test KSF-Chol against reference solvers and numerical reference data on multiple 2D and 3D benchmarks and demonstrate a significantly reduced numerical diffusion as well as a competitive accuracy concerning the computation of relevant flow quantities.
item.dc:creator: L. Scholz, A. Bacho, H. Owhadi

item.title: Quadrature Perturbations and High-Order Time Discretization for Prescribed-Feature Evolutionary GTransNet Galerkin Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.03281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study quadrature perturbations and high-order time discretization for a prescribed-feature evolutionary generalized transferable neural network (Evo-GTransNet) Galerkin method for linear self-adjoint parabolic equations. Assembly quadrature, together with truncated singular value decomposition, is used to select a numerically resolved trial space and obtain coordinates with an identity mass matrix. Since this normalization depends on the assembly quadrature, the retained functions are also evaluated using a separate comparison quadrature, which is finer in the numerical experiments. For the two resulting semidiscrete systems, we derive an exact equation for the difference between their trajectories and an energy estimate that separates errors arising from the effective operator, load vector, and initial projection. The estimate is conditional on the trial space selected by the assembly quadrature. The retained rank, discarded mass, cross mass, and principal angles are used to assess this selection step. Refining the comparison quadrature yields stable retained spaces for the reported configurations, whereas deliberate underintegration leads to much larger perturbations. On the fixed retained systems, the temporal convergence of implicit midpoint, BDF, Radau IIA, and Gauss--Legendre methods is consistent with their classical orders over the resolved refinement ranges. The experiments distinguish the retained-coordinate error from the total solution error; the latter is measured against the PDE solution in the $L^2$ norm, with the error integrals evaluated by sufficiently fine quadrature. They also illustrate the importance of suitable starting values for BDF3 and show how the performance of IMEX-BDF schemes depends on the operator splitting and time step size.
item.dc:creator: Xi Zhang, Lili Ju, Jin Zhao

item.title: Scalable Fully Implicit Runge-Kutta Solvers for Time-Dependent Rayleigh-B\'enard Convection
item.description: arXiv:2611.03361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the efficient numerical solution of time-dependent Rayleigh-B\'enard convection governed by the incompressible Boussinesq equations. The coupled velocity-pressure-temperature system presents significant computational challenges arising from incompressibility, buoyancy coupling, convection, and the simultaneous resolution of multiple physical time scales. We present a systematic study of fully implicit Runge-Kutta methods for time-dependent Rayleigh-B\'enard convection, together with scalable finite element solvers for the resulting stage-coupled systems. We employ high-order, L-stable Radau IIA methods for temporal integration and investigate Taylor-Hood and Alfeld-Sorokina finite elements in two dimensions, along with Taylor-Hood and enriched macroelement discretizations in three dimensions. The macroelement approaches offer strong local inf-sup stability and patch structures well suited to Vanka-type relaxation. In two dimensions, monolithic multigrid achieves nearly stage-independent outer Krylov iteration counts and maintains robust convergence under mesh refinement. On the same mesh with incremental pressure correction, selected Radau configurations reduce elapsed solve time by 18-32% and yield smaller sampled transient differences relative to a numerical reference solution. Three-dimensional experiments demonstrate favorable parallel scalability with Taylor-Hood elements and substantially improved discrete mass conservation with the enriched macroelement discretization. These results identify regimes in which coupled multistage fully implicit integration is computationally competitive when equipped with appropriate multigrid preconditioners.
item.dc:creator: Ahsan Ali, Robert C. Kirby

item.title: Optimal bounds for design curves on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2611.03362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A closed rectifiable curve on the torus $\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d$ is a $t$-design curve if normalized arclength integration is exact for trigonometric polynomials $e^{2\pi i \langle m,x\rangle}$ with frequencies $m\in\mathbb Z^d$ satisfying $\|m\|_\infty\le t$. For the arclength $L$ of such curves, we establish the sharp lower bound \begin{equation}\label{eq:abs} L\geq \Big(\frac{(t+1)^{2d}-1}{t(t+2)}\Big)^{1/2}. \end{equation} Equality is attained by the family of Korobov curves described in \cite{Kunis,Lindblad}. For even $t$, we also derive an explicit lower bound on the length of total-degree $t$-design curves, defined by the frequency condition $\|m\|_1\leq t$. This bound is sharp for $t=2$ in every dimension and for every even $t$ in dimension two. We determine the minimum length of hyperbolic cross $t^2$-design curves in dimension two. For $d\geq3$, we establish lower bounds of optimal order for the length of hyperbolic cross $t^d$-design curves. Finally, we obtain lower bounds of optimal order for the length of $t$-design curves associated with sparse frequency sets.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ehler

item.title: First- and second-order constrained optimisation for inverse homogenisation of unidirectionally varying microstructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.03372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with inverse homogenisation problems that aim to identify microstructure features of a body from macroscopic measurements. The unknown microstructure is assumed to vary macroscopically in one spatial direction and affects the effective tensor in an elliptic partial differential equation that governs the behaviour of the body on the macroscale. We establish the well-posedness of the PDE-constrained minimisation problems that model the task of identifying the microstructure, derive first-order necessary optimality conditions, and prove the convergence of a gradient-projection algorithm for the studied problem class in an infinite-dimensional setting. We moreover demonstrate that recently obtained results on generalised differentiability properties of solution maps of bilateral obstacle problems make it possible to set up and analyse a novel semismooth Newton method in the considered situation. The functional analytic setting that we use for our investigation is chosen such that it covers various elliptic PDEs simultaneously (classical second-order equations, bi-Laplace problems, linear elasticity, etc.) and explicitly exploits the problem structure to obtain global convergence guarantees for the studied solution algorithms in terms of the Lipschitz constants of the involved operators. Our analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments which show that the new semismooth Newton approach requires far less expensive projection evaluations than the gradient-descent method and, thus, offers a significant speedup.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Christof, Malte A. Peter, Michael Ulbrich

item.title: Rate optimality of AFEM with maximum marking
item.description: arXiv:2611.03387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For Poisson's equation, we prove optimal algebraic convergence rates for adaptive conforming finite element methods driven by standard maximum marking in arbitrary space dimension, for every marking parameter in $(0,1]$. Previously, instance optimality of a modified maximum marking was proved in [L. Diening, C. Kreuzer, and R. Stevenson, Instance optimality of the adaptive maximum strategy, Found. Comput. Math., 16 (2016), pp. 33--68]. The basic ingredients of our anlaysis consists of discrete reliability, discrete efficiency, overlay and closure estimates of local mesh refinement. The discrete efficiency requires a facet-interior node property of simplicial mesh refinement. The novel part of the optimality analysis is an elementary integral-sum argument that converts energy decrease into a cumulative cardinality bound of marked elements, yielding rate optimality without a contraction argument.
item.dc:creator: Yuwen Li

item.title: Two-level additive Schwarz preconditioners with GDSW coarse spaces for high-order discretizations in 3D
item.description: arXiv:2611.03447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Overlapping Schwarz methods are among the most successful domain decomposition preconditioners for large-scale finite element simulations. In this work, the Generalized Dryja-Smith-Widlund (GDSW), GDSW$^*$, and Reduced GDSW (RGDSW) coarse spaces are studied for three-dimensional high-order finite element method (FEM) and virtual element method (VEM) for the Poisson equation and the equations of linear elasticity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study of GDSW-type coarse spaces for polynomial degrees $k\ge 3$ in three dimensions, for either discretization. In 3D VEM, the face degrees of freedom (DOFs) are moments instead of point values. The kernel of the differential operator, which defines the interface values of the GDSW coarse basis functions, must be represented through these moments. The construction is therefore no longer purely algebraic and, without this correction, the coarse level loses its effect for $k\ge 3$. FEM and VEM are tested on hexahedral meshes, and VEM is additionally tested on polyhedral ones. Polynomial degrees up to $k=5$ and runs on up to $4\,096$ subdomains and parallel cores are included in the numerical study. Numerical experiments show scalable iteration counts for all coarse space variants for the Poisson problem, illustrating the expected trade-off between the coarse space size and robustness. Further experiments for linear elasticity confirms that the moment-based construction extends naturally from the scalar to the vector-valued problem.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Bevilacqua, Axel Klawonn, Martin Lanser, Adam Wasiak

item.title: Lattice Green's functions for Poisson problems with two unbounded and one periodic direction
item.description: arXiv:2611.03458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fourier-based Poisson solvers treat periodic directions spectrally and unbounded ones by the Hockney--Eastwood convolution with a free-space kernel. With two unbounded and one periodic direction, the setting of vortex tubes, wakes and jets, the kernel used so far by these solvers combines the two-dimensional kernel on the zero periodic mode with the symbol of the operator sampled on the doubled grid on every other mode. We show that the second ingredient is not exact: the error is the field of the periodic images of the source and independent of the mesh size. While the period $L_z$ is not much longer than the unbounded extent $L_x$, it is of order $\exp(-2\pi d/L_z)$, with $d$ the distance to the nearest image; beyond, it grows like $(L_z/L_x)^2$. The error is thus small on cubic domains, but larger than the solution itself on elongated ones. We remove the approximation by extending the integral representation of the exact second-order kernel of Hou and Colonius: the screened kernel of each mode is evaluated in closed form along one unbounded direction and by Gauss--Legendre quadrature along the other, for the high-order dimension-split and Mehrstellen stencils, at a one-off cost of about one solve. The kernels, implemented in the open-source library \flups{}, are verified by comparison with independent quadratures, by a padding test sensitive to the boundary condition enforced, and by convergence at the order of each stencil on an axially modulated tube source, on domains up to $64$ times longer than wide and up to $2.7\times10^{11}$ unknowns.
item.dc:creator: Gilles Poncelet, Philippe Chatelain

item.title: Symbol-based residual certification of reduced and neural surrogates for tempered-fractional CGMY pricing
item.description: arXiv:2611.03463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We certify reduced and neural approximations of European-put price trajectories under the Carr--Geman--Madan--Yor model by residual bounds for the spline Galerkin discretisation of the tempered-fractional pricing equation. The Galerkin matrices are Toeplitz sections of an explicit periodised Fourier symbol; summing the alias series to a stated tail makes the assembled system exact to $10^{-8}$. A L\'evy--Khintchine argument gives the parameter-explicit bound $\lambda_{\min}(S_I)\ge r\,m_{\min}$ for the symmetric part, valid for $Y\in(0,2)\setminus\{1\}$, replacing numerical spectral estimates. A banded comparison norm built from the mass and stiffness symbols yields a rigorous certificate at $O(N)$ cost with explicit effectivity, and empirical interpolation of the symbol makes the operator affine in about 36 terms with a rigorous error transfer, so a reduced model is certified at a cost independent of $N$; a three-stage rule escalates to the full-order bounds only when needed. At the resolution that prices the whole parameter box to one cent ($N=1024$), the full-order certificate costs 6% of a direct solve, and the certified POD--Galerkin model of rank 80 costs 3% of it and settles 99.8% of $10^4$ queries without touching the full space. No false accept occurs on any query with a reference solution (150 inside the parameter box, 264 outside), and outside the box the certificate accepts 193 of the 210 queries on which the reduced model is still within one cent. The neural reduced models trained here miss the one-cent tolerance by a factor of at least 46; the certificate detects this at every query in a few milliseconds and explains it as a trade-off between temporal smoothness and coefficient accuracy. A residual certificate for the American put is proved as an outlook.
item.dc:creator: Davood Damircheli

item.title: An Active Flux Method for Maxwell's equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a novel Active Flux method and a divergence-free method using exact evolution operators for solving Maxwell's equations in three space dimensions on Cartesian grids. The proposed methods are fully discrete, third-order accurate and rely on a truly multidimensional evolution operator based on Kirchhoff's formula for the electromagnetic wave equation. The first method is a classical Active Flux method with globally continuous reconstruction while the second method is an adaptation of the Active Flux method to a locally divergence-free reconstruction by Balsara. The applied reconstruction is built from facial degrees of freedom and is no longer globally continuous. The classical method keeps the divergence error bounded. The divergence-free method with face averages initialized by a potential keeps the constraints at round-off. We compare the accuracy of both methods for smooth and discontinuous test problems.
item.dc:creator: Yanick Kiechle, Christiane Helzel

item.title: Structured Neural Network Models for Anisotropic Magnetic Constitutive Laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.03475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-performance electrical steel used for iron cores of power transformers and generators exhibits complex material behavior. While modeling and simulation of isotropic nonlinear response is well understood, the incorporation of magnetic anisotropy remains challenging. This work proposes to utilize a structured neural network architecture to systematically describe the anisotropic nonlinear anhysteretic magnetic material response of electrical steel sheets. By constructing a convex and smooth co-energy density with dedicated behavior at infinity, we can ensure thermodynamic consistency and correct physical behavior and further guarantee basic mathematical properties which provide well-posedness of corresponding magnetic field problems and efficient numerical solvers. Numerical tests demonstrate the capability of the proposed method to describe strongly anisotropic behavior as well as its robust convergence in finite-element simulations.
item.dc:creator: Dorian Zeilinger, Felix Engertsberger, Herbert Egger

item.title: High-order in-cell discontinuous reconstruction path-conservative methods for conservative systems in primitive variables
item.description: arXiv:2611.03479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a path-conservative methodology for the numerical approximation of conservative systems formulated exclusively in primitive variables, the most physically relevant set of variables. The approach is designed to preserve the correct weak solution while avoiding the spurious oscillations near contact discontinuities that may arise in conservative formulations. Nonconservative products are treated through the selection of a suitable family of paths combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction strategy, which is locally activated near shocks. To choose the path we introduce a compatibility condition between the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions of the non-conservative form, with the exact ones, assumed to be known. In smooth regions and across contact discontinuities, a standard path-conservative scheme is employed. The method is further extended to achieve high-order accuracy. Numerical results for the Euler multimaterial and shear interface model demonstrates correct shock-capturing property, suppression of spurious oscillations due to contact discontinuities, and convergence without using hybrid formulations.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Pimentel-Garc\'ia, Mario Ricchiuto, Carlos Par\'es

item.title: High-order guaranteed lower bounds for the Schr\"odinger eigenvalue problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.03567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute unconditional guaranteed lower eigenvalue bounds for Schr\"odinger operators using a modified hybrid high-order method with built-in correction for the potential defect. The method assumes exact numerical integration and allows possibly unbounded potentials in $L^p$ for $p>n/2$ and $p\geq2$ on general polyhedral domains. We prove that the high-order correction preserves optimal a priori convergence orders, and derive reliable and efficient a posteriori error estimators. Numerical experiments provide striking evidence of optimal high-order convergence rates of the adaptive algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Benedikt Gr\"a{\ss}le, Moritz Hauck, Yizhou Liang

item.title: Multi-Trajectory Parallel-in-Iteration Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Previously, we developed a ``parallel-in-iteration'' optimization framework that uses multigrid reduction-in-time (MGRIT) to parallelize slowly converging optimization methods, such as gradient descent. Unlike time-dependent evolution problems, optimization requires only a final point with a sufficiently small gradient, rather than an accurate approximation of the entire trajectory of iterates. This motivates a different use of MGRIT: instead of repeatedly improving the approximation of a single long trajectory, we introduce restarted MGRIT (R-MGRIT), which performs one MGRIT iteration on a trajectory, takes the approximate final point as a new initial guess, and repeats the process on a new trajectory. Each restart thus defines a new all-at-once system, allowing progress toward the solution without accurately approximating the preceding trajectory. Moreover, we find that these trajectories can be shortened without increasing the number of restarts needed for convergence. We provide theoretical results comparing MGRIT and R-MGRIT for linear problems and demonstrate the convergence behavior of the shortened trajectories numerically for both linear and nonlinear problems. Shortening the trajectories increases the estimated parallel speedup while reducing the number of processors required.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme H. M. Araujo, Oliver A. Krzysik, Hans De Sterck

item.title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
item.description: arXiv:2610.41778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatially resolved modeling of optically pumped alkali-metal vapors requires the solution of a high-dimensional nonlinear diffusive quantum master equation (DQME) coupled to state-dependent light propagation. We develop a structure-preserving computational framework for this coupled three-dimensional system in the high-pressure limit.
