The high-fidelity solver combines second-order finite differences, explicit pseudo-time marching, and an exponential-integrator discretization of the light-propagation equation. The scheme preserves the density-matrix trace, while a derived global pseudo-time-step restriction guarantees nonnegative, bound-preserving population updates and frozen-coefficient $1$-norm stability. In the absence of a closed-form solution for the general coupled problem, the solver is verified against complementary analytical reductions, pumping-rate asymptotics, and a light-propagation invariant, all of which are accurately recovered. Tensorized GPU implementation reduces the per-iteration cost by more than two orders of magnitude relative to a single-core CPU. For repeated parameter queries, we further construct an intrusive POD--Galerkin reduced-order model. The quadratic spin-exchange term is treated by an exact nonlinear quadratic expansion, whereas the nonpolynomial and nonlocal optical-pumping term is hyper-reduced using the discrete empirical interpolation method. At out-of-sample parameter points, the reduced model closely reproduces the full-order population and polarization fields while achieving speedup of more than \(7\times10^3\) relative to the single-core CPU full-order solver. The resulting hierarchy connects verified high-fidelity simulation with efficient reduced-order prediction for spatially resolved alkali-metal spin dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Keyu Xu, Kezheng Yan, Jinbo Hu, Yanqing Shi, Xiaorui Xu, Nan Zhao, Qian Wang

item.title: DiffStent: Surrogate Adjoint Differentiation for Stent Deployment in Anisotropic Arteries
item.description: arXiv:2611.00014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present DiffStent, a differentiable finite element framework for simulating arterial deformation during in silico stent deployment, where nearly incompressible, anisotropic vessel walls undergo large deformation and frictional contact with the stent. DiffStent combines the fiber-reinforced Holzapfel-Gasser-Ogden constitutive model with an implicit discrete adjoint that differentiates the converged mechanical equilibrium without unrolling the nonlinear solver, thus reducing the memory cost by three orders of magnitude. We identify three mechanisms that can lead to inaccurate, unstable, or uninformative gradients: nonsmooth switching, state mismatch, and gradient cancellation. To address these, we apply a contact surrogate in the backward pass while retaining the original physical model in the forward pass. We show superior gradient accuracy of our method over AutoDiff and finite differencing across constitutive benchmarks, idealized stented vessels, and patient-specific calcified coronary anatomies, and use the resulting sensitivities to quantify how tissue properties and calcification patterns govern lumen expansion and arterial wall stress. Finally, we demonstrate that DiffStent enables gradient-based system identification from retrospective clinical images of atherosclerotic coronary anatomy. Together, these results establish a practical approach for differentiating through nonlinear biomechanical simulations with stiff constitutive laws and nonsmooth contact, enabling patient-specific parameter inference and optimization in computational cardiovascular mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Shoaib A. Goraya, Ajay Manicka, Aviral Jain, Karim Kadry, Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Elazer R. Edelman, Farhad R. Nezami

item.title: A Preconditioned Semismooth Newton Method for Box-Constrained Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Random Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.00246v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the optimal control problem of an elliptic PDE with random diffusion under pointwise box constraints on the control. The constraints make the optimality conditions nonsmooth, with an active set that is not known in advance, and the random diffusion couples the state and the adjoint across all stochastic modes. To design a solution algorithm for this problem, we rely on the Fenchel duality viewpoint. Fenchel duality absorbs the box constraint into the objective and yields an exact reduced problem in the elliptic adjoint variable alone. After a stochastic Galerkin--finite element discretization, eliminating the state leaves a strongly monotone, piecewise smooth equation, which we solve directly by a matrix-free semismooth Newton method with the box projection retained exactly and with no outer iteration, penalty or smoothing parameter. Next, we introduce and analyze a current-set preconditioner, which adds the active-set correction of the current Newton step to a mean-diffusion reference operator and is inverted exactly by a rank-1 update. For implementation, we use a cheaper preconditioner that keeps only a fraction of free control values. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence of the state, and Newton and PCG counts that stay bounded under mesh refinement and growth of the stochastic dimension.
item.dc:creator: Zhendong Li, Akwum Onwunta, Hailing Wang

item.title: The Rise of Low Precision Floating Point
item.description: arXiv:2611.00301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Floating point computing has dominated scientific computations since the 1950s because of its versatile ability to approximate real numbers with both sufficiently high precision and sufficiently great range. Since 1985, two specific formats have become standard across the industry, one with 32 bits which is adequate for many purposes and one with 64 bits which allows numbers with both much higher precision and much greater range for applications where these are needed. However, during the past decade, deep learning has come to dominate computation, and narrower floating point formats with lower precision and reduced range have steadily become more common. In this article we discuss this phenomenon, why it is happening, how various 16-bit, 8-bit and even 4-bit floating point formats have been developed, and efforts to standardize these formats.
item.dc:creator: Guy Lemieux, Michael L. Overton

item.title: Learning to evolve by matching velocities
item.description: arXiv:2611.00448v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning the continuous-time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems relies on trajectory-based objectives, which require simulating the learned dynamics during training and backpropagating through the numerical scheme, at a cost that grows with the rollout horizon. We show that trajectory-based objectives degenerate as the rollout horizon increases, hindering gradient-based optimization, and that the numerical scheme biases the learned dynamics by constraining the spectrum of the learned Jacobian to its absolute stability region. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Velocity Matching (VM), a simulation-free objective that relies on piecewise-linear interpolation and stochastic collocation, and approximates the velocity population risk to second order in the sampling step. We develop a theoretical framework for velocity-based learning, introducing stability estimates that control trajectory errors in terms of velocity errors, which enable us to establish universal and continuous-time approximation results when the learned velocity field is parameterized by deep neural networks. Building on a bias-variance decomposition of the VM objective, we show that its higher-order approximation of the velocity population risk yields a consistent minimizer; that it relates to the residual of an A-stable continuous-stage Runge-Kutta scheme, thus connecting VM to implicit integration without requiring any implicit solve; and that it implicitly matches the action of the learned Jacobian to that of the true one along the observed trajectories, without requiring access to the underlying velocity field or its Jacobian. Numerical experiments on nonlinear ordinary differential equations and semi-discretized time-dependent partial differential equations show that VM improves accuracy over trajectory-based objectives, while avoiding both the cost of simulation and the instabilities of long rollouts.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Farenga, Andrea Manzoni

item.title: Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.00721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surface parameterization is a fundamental task in geometry processing and shape analysis. For topologically closed surfaces, it is common to parameterize them onto a standardized closed domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a prime example being a unit sphere for genus-0 closed surfaces. Many mapping methods use planar projections and perform computations on the plane rather than directly on the 3D surface. However, perturbations introduced before projection or geometric evolution propagate through the computation and may affect map quality, convergence, stopping behavior, and geometric validity. In this work, we formulate representation sensitivity as a branchwise input--output problem, separating smooth propagation through active Jacobians from changes in anchors, stopping rules, and fallback events. Under consistent piecewise-linear assembly, the unmodified south-pole Beltrami correction in the FLASH method for spherical conformal parameterization reduces exactly to source-mesh harmonic extension. On a fixed-anchor branch, the corrected map factors into chart transition, harmonic propagation, and inverse stereographic projection, yielding an explicit sensitivity Jacobian and a finite-triangle conditioning bound. Separately, we introduce a bounded five-parameter affine preconditioner over planar scale, translation, and anisotropy and evaluate candidates on the corrected spherical map. Across 30 genus-0 surfaces, it reduces median polar upper-tail log-condition and chord-angle distortion by $10.17\%$ and $10.97\%$, respectively, with both measures improving on every mesh. We also apply the framework to other spherical mapping methods including the conformalized mean-curvature flow and spherical density-equalizing maps. Altogether, our work highlights the importance of representation selection as a structural and practical component of spherical parameterization and downstream computation.
item.dc:creator: Zixi Yi, Gary P. T. Choi

item.title: Unbiased Low-Rank Approximation for Repeated Matrix-Vector Multiplication: Stability and Optimal Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.00787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Replacing the matrix in an iteration with random low-rank matrices can reduce the cost of matrix-vector multiplication. However, even if the sampled matrices equal the original matrix in expectation, the expected squared norm of the random iterates may grow while the original iteration converges. Under a fixed rank bound, we study how to choose the distribution of these random matrices to minimize this growth when sampling independently at each step. We derive an exact formula for the optimal asymptotic growth factor and use it to determine when the expected squared norm can converge to zero. We then characterize precisely when a fixed sampling distribution achieves this optimal factor and construct finite-support optimal distributions in every attainable case. These results determine the minimum rank required for stability and provide optimal sampling designs under the prescribed rank constraint.
item.dc:creator: Kang Liu

item.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.00922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a Gaussian Mixture (GM) representation of a full-dimensional subset of Euclidean space with finite volume from a finite simplicial triangulation in closed form. On each simplex, we replace the uniform probability density function (PDF) with a Gaussian PDF that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, arriving at the information projection onto the family of Gaussian PDFs. By exploiting affine isomorphisms between simplices, the joint convexity and bijection invariance properties of the KL divergence, identities for Dirichlet PDFs, and a partition-of-unity argument, we establish a dimension-dependent but geometry-independent sharp upper bound on the global KL divergence between the resulting GM PDF and the uniform PDF on the original domain. Numerical examples illustrate the construction and demonstrate its potential in practical applications.
item.dc:creator: Ali Darijani, Benedikt Stratmann, Uwe D. Hanebeck, Ratan Bahadur Thapa, J\"urgen Beyerer, Nehal Afifi

item.title: Accelerating posterior sampling in Bayesian inverse problems with diffusion models: an online-offline perspective
item.description: arXiv:2611.01300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayesian inverse problems require both informative prior models and computationally feasible posterior inference. Score-based diffusion models provide expressive learned priors, but their use for inversion introduces a conditioning problem: the score of a noised posterior is generally unavailable from a prior score alone. This selective survey reviews the principal approaches to that problem, including likelihood guidance, spectral and projection methods, sequential Monte Carlo corrections, and amortized conditional training. We organize methods by how they split cost between offline preparation and online inference, and compare their assumptions, advantages and limitations, with emphasis on computational speedups. Some ongoing directions and open questions are gathered at the end.
item.dc:creator: Duc-Lam Duong

item.title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.01432v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.
item.dc:creator: Pei Ge, Huan Lei

item.title: Tensor Contraction with ZX Calculus, a Graph-Theoretic Approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.01890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tensors are higher dimensional generalisations of vectors and matrices. Tensor networks are a diagrammatic representation of complicated relations between tensors, and tensor contraction is the evaluation of a tensor network analogous to matrix multiplication. Tensor networks and tensor contraction are ubiquitous in computer science, physics, and applied mathematics. Most existing tensor contraction algorithms are focused on finding an optimal contraction order of the tensors' bonds. However, finding the optimal order is an NP-hard problem. It is equivalent to another possibly more straightforward but still NP-hard problem of finding the treewidth of the line graph of the tensor network. While in general finding the optimal bond-by-bond contraction order is hard, in many practical cases there is no need to find an optimal order. This observation leads to the core innovation of this thesis, which is a new tensor contraction paradigm that uses graph theoretic operations to produce an equivalent tensor network whose line graph has lower treewidth than the original tensor network, before applying the bond-by-bond contraction algorithm. We call these graph theoretical operations \textit{rewrite preprocessing}, and we name the algorithms that apply rewrite preprocessing before regular bond-by-bond contraction \textit{Tensor Contraction with Graph Operation}. There are many possible ways to perform rewrite preprocessing; in this thesis, we focus on the graph operations of ZX calculus, a diagrammatic language for quantum circuits. Ample numerical simulations have been performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Yuhao Han

item.title: Optimal asymptotic bounds for design curves on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.01895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A spherical $t$-design is a finite set of points on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere such that averaging any polynomial of degree at most $t$ over these points gives its exact spherical average. We study the corresponding notion for curves, where point averages are replaced by normalized arclength integration. For fixed $d\ge 2$, the length of such curves is known to be bounded below by a positive multiple of $t^{d-1}$ as $t\to\infty$. We show that this asymptotic order is attained: for every $d\ge 2$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that, for every positive integer $t$ and every prescribed length $L\ge C_dt^{d-1}$, there is a simple spherical $t$-design curve of length $L$. This establishes the analogue for curves of the theorem of Bondarenko, Radchenko, and Viazovska, which resolved the Korevaar-Meyers conjecture for spherical design points. More generally, we prove the corresponding result on closed, connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension $d\ge 2$, where eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator substitute for polynomials. The proof combines a geometric construction of curves with continuously adjustable local lengths and an application of Brouwer's degree theorem.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ehler

item.title: Black Hole Love Numbers with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.02084v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop and validate a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for computing the tidal Love numbers of black holes directly from their perturbation equations. We consider static perturbations of the Kerr black hole, whose exact hypergeometric solutions provide a controlled benchmark for both the numerical solver and the extraction of the physical response. The framework combines exact enforcement of the horizon boundary conditions with an $H^2$-Sobolev loss that incorporates derivatives of the differential-equation residual. The Love number is then obtained by extracting the asymptotic coefficients of the learned solution, without using the analytic connection formula. Across the tested scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations, the method recovers the finite dissipative response with relative errors below $10^{-5}$. Controlled comparisons show that the higher-derivative loss terms improve solution accuracy by orders of magnitude, while independent tests of the extraction procedure distinguish solver errors from errors in recovering the response coefficients. The conservative response, which vanishes analytically, is constrained by the numerical error floor. These results demonstrate that PINNs can accurately compute black-hole tidal response and establish a validated framework for future extensions to frequency-dependent and non-separable perturbation problems.
item.dc:creator: Maria J. Rodriguez, Luis Fernando Temoche, Pavlos Protopapas

item.title: Accelerating phase-field simulations of grain growth via tensor decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.02118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Phase-field models provide a powerful framework for simulating grain growth phenomena in polycrystalline materials, but their application to large-scale systems is limited by the high computational and memory costs associated with resolving multiple phase variables over fine spatial and temporal scales. This paper presents a tensor decomposition based model reduction framework for accelerating phase-field simulations of grain growth. The proposed method exploits the underlying low-rank structure of the evolving phase-field variables and represents the high-dimensional solution in a spatially decomposed tensor format. By performing the numerical computations directly within this reduced representation, the framework decreases storage requirements and reduces the cost of repeatedly solving the phase-field equations. The number of modes for the decomposed approximation is controlled during the online computation with a subspace mode-updating algorithm, to balance computational efficiency and approximation accuracy. The method is assessed using representative grain growth problems, and its predictions are compared with those obtained from conventional full-order finite element simulations. The results demonstrate that the formulation can accurately reproduce the evolution of grain morphology and the principal characteristics of grain growth kinetics while substantially improving computational efficiency. The proposed framework therefore provides a promising approach for extending phase-field simulations to larger spatial domains, finer discretizations, and systems containing a large number of phase variables.
item.dc:creator: Chaoqian Yuan, Dingxiang Zhu, Ye Lu

item.title: A Unified Space-Time Variational Framework for Wave Equations on Differential Forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.02136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit a standard space--time variational formulation of the scalar wave equation in the setting of differential forms. For this, we use as spatial operator the nonnegative, self-adjoint (relative) \emph{Hodge--Laplacian} on a bounded Lipschitz domain. Its spectral decomposition reduces the wave problem in any form degree to the same family of scalar ordinary differential equations that underlies existing space-time analysis. We illustrate how this can be used to transfer results from the scalar wave equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions to other wave-type problems. In particular, we connect the framework to perfectly electrically conducting Maxwell problems.
item.dc:creator: C. Urz\'ua-Torres, A. Wisse

item.title: Comparison Principle and Semi-Lagrangian Methods for a Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman System with Recursive Utility
item.description: arXiv:2611.02763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a system of coupled first-order Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations arising in continuous-time heterogeneous agent models with recursive utility, a class of models that has attracted increasing attention in macroeconomics. The first part of the paper establishes a comparison principle for the system when preferences exhibit early resolution of uncertainty. A key ingredient in the proof is an ordinally equivalent transformation of the recursive utility representation. In the second part, we develop semi-Lagrangian schemes and iterative algorithms for solving the associated nonlinear discrete systems. For preferences exhibiting late resolution of uncertainty, we establish a first-order error estimate for the semi-Lagrangian approximation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods yield results consistent with those obtained using the previously developed finite difference schemes.
item.dc:creator: Qing Tang

item.title: Pollutant Concentration Reconstruction in Porous Media from Localized Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.02864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable environmental monitoring and groundwater protection heavily rely on the ability to reconstruct full pollutant concentration fields from sparse, partial field measurements. In porous media, dissolved contaminants are transported by groundwater flow while undergoing hydrodynamic dispersion and complex chemical or biological reactions. To address practical contamination challenges, this work investigates the reconstruction of pollutant distributions using water samples collected at discrete locations in unsaturated or saturated soils via sampling tubes equipped with ceramic tips. While these suction samplers provide critical local data, they inherently capture only a fraction of the subsurface environment, leaving wide areas unmonitored. Motivated by this real-world monitoring procedure, we propose steady and time-dependent advection-diffusion-reaction models to simulate contaminant transport. Our main contribution is a generalized unique continuation result demonstrating that, under appropriate physical and mathematical assumptions, two concentration fields coinciding on a non-empty observation region must match throughout the entire space-time domain, even when originating from different source configurations. We investigate this problem from both theoretical and numerical perspectives, backing our mathematical uniqueness results with numerical simulations that validate the efficiency and practical utility of our approach. The theoretical proofs combine regularity properties away from source singularities with unique-continuation principles for parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, providing a robust framework for environmental risk assessment and site remediation.
item.dc:creator: Adel Blouza, Siyu Cen, Yavar Kian

item.title: Low-rank corrections to a shared reference Jacobian for GPU-parallel AC $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.03012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Contingency analysis repeatedly solves the power-flow equations under many single-element outages, an increasingly demanding workload as operating margins tighten and renewable variability grows. Graphics processing units (GPUs) are attractive for this task, but a change in topology alters the sparsity pattern of the Jacobian, preventing the uniform batched factorization on which efficient GPU solvers rely. This paper presents a GPU-parallel Newton--Raphson solver for $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis that separates the change in operating state from the change in topology. A single reference Jacobian is inverted once and reused across all contingencies. Each topology change is expressed as a low-rank Woodbury correction, while the residual state-dependent perturbation is handled by an inner iterative solve, a truncated Neumann series or the biconjugate gradient stabilized method. We analyze the spectral radius and condition number of the resulting iteration matrices and show that the reference Jacobian is an effective preconditioner. On transmission-scale benchmarks, the method attains per-topology solve times competitive with an optimized 80-core central processing unit baseline, with the low-rank correction accounting for approximately 1--2\% of the workload. This makes GPU-parallel $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis feasible at transmission scale without per-topology refactorization.
item.dc:creator: Marc Hunkem\"oller, Nico Westerbeck, Joost van Dijk, Lars Schewe, Dirk Witthaut

item.title: Scaling global tractography with ExaTract: from large cohorts to ultra-high-resolution datasets
item.description: arXiv:2611.03419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Global tractography offers a theoretical framework for reconstructing white matter connectivity from diffusion MRI by jointly inferring all streamlines and their consistency with the diffusion signal and underlying anatomical priors. However, its sequential nature and log-linear complexity make it computationally prohibitive at the scales demanded by neuroimaging, from large population cohorts such as the Human Connectome Project (HCP) to ex vivo ultra-high-field acquisitions at mesoscopic resolution. In this work, we present ExaTract, a parallelized spin-glass tractography framework designed for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Implemented as an open-source MPI+Kokkos application, ExaTract partitions the tractography domain into spatially overlapping regions processed across distributed memory nodes, with regular synchronization of boundary modifications to preserve global convergence guarantees. We validate ExaTract on both in vivo and ex vivo diffusion MRI data: the complete HCP dataset demonstrates population-scale throughput, while the high-resolution Chenonceau dataset provides the first mesoscopic structural connectome derived from global tractography.
item.dc:creator: Simon Legeay, Felix Matuschke, Bastien Herlin, Jan Andr\'e Reuter, Christophe Destrieux, Markus Axer, Ivy Uszynski, Cyril Poupon

item.title: Unrolled gradients in disguise: bridging interpolation-based and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.03461v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hybrid models and neural differential equations (NDEs) are becoming increasingly important for modelling physical systems; however, they often encounter stability and accuracy issues during long-term integration. Training on unrolled trajectories is known to limit these divergences but quickly becomes too computationally expensive due to the need to compute gradients over an iterative process, making this method impractical for large-scale physical systems (e.g. weather and climate forecasting). Two popular paradigms for improving the stability of learned dynamics are to train on interpolated or noisy samples or to regularize the Jacobian of the learned representation. In this work, we demonstrate that these paradigms can be understood under a common lens and that they both correspond to an approximation of the gradients obtained in an unrolled learning strategy. Building on this understanding, we derive a principled and complete approach to regularize training and demonstrate its impact on the stability of learned dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Maya Janvier, Etienne Meunier

item.title: A hyperbolic nonlinear Schr\"odinger system in multiple spatial dimensions: structure, convergence, and numerical discretization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03642v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose and study a first-order hyperbolic approximation of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation in $N$ spatial dimensions. This is an extension of the recently-proposed 1D hyperbolic NLS model. We study the structure and properties of the hyperbolic approximation and their relation to those of the original system. We show that the N-dimensional hyperbolic system exactly conserves analogs of the mass, energy, and momentum, and that it possesses stationary solutions that are closely related to those of NLS. The hyperbolic system is also shown to admit plane-wave solutions that share some stability properties with those of NLS, and that relaxation can shrink the focusing low-wavenumber modulational instability band as well as introduce a high-wavenumber instability band not present in NLS. We also show that solutions of the hyperbolic system converge to solutions of NLS in the relaxation limit. We present an adaptive-mesh finite volume discretization of the hyperbolic system and demonstrate its effectiveness in handling simulations, including those with geometric obstacles or non-periodic boundary conditions. The effectiveness of the numerical scheme is demonstrated through examples including a Bose-Einstein condensate, line soliton instability, and superflow past a cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Mu\~noz-Moncayo, Abhijit Biswas, David I. Ketcheson, Manvendra Rajvanshi

item.title: Neural numerical homogenization based on Deep Ritz corrections
item.description: arXiv:2411.14084v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Numerical homogenization methods aim at providing appropriate coarse-scale approximations of solutions to (elliptic) partial differential equations that involve highly oscillatory coefficients. The localized orthogonal decomposition (LOD) method is an effective way of dealing with such coefficients, especially if they are non-periodic and non-smooth. It modifies classical finite element basis functions by suitable fine-scale corrections. In this paper, we make use of the structure of the LOD method, but we propose to calculate the corrections based on a Deep Ritz approach involving a parametrization of the coefficients to tackle temporal variations or uncertainties. Numerical examples for a parabolic model problem are presented to assess the performance of the approach.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Elasmi, Felix Krumbiegel, Roland Maier

item.title: Mixed-precision iterative refinement for low-rank Lyapunov equations
item.description: arXiv:2510.02126v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a mixed-precision iterative refinement framework for solving low-rank Lyapunov matrix equations $AX + XA^T + W =0$, where $W=LL^T$ or $W=LSL^T$. Via rounding error analysis of the algorithms we derive sufficient conditions for the attainable normwise residuals in different precision settings and show how the algorithmic parameters should be chosen. These conditions are independent of the choice of inner solver, provided that the prescribed residual accuracy is attained in the inner solves. Using the sign-function Newton iteration as the solver, we demonstrate that reduced precisions, such as half precision with unit roundoff $u_s$, can be used for Lyapunov equations with condition number of order $u_s^{-1}$ without compromising the attainable solution quality. The numerical experiments validate our error analysis, and we establish cost models to quantify the expected speedup for different low-to-high precision timing ratios. This work provides an algorithmic framework towards exploiting native low-precision hardware to accelerate low-rank Lyapunov solvers without sacrificing accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Peter Benner, Xiaobo Liu

item.title: Inverse Iterations for Phase-Invariant Nonlinear Eigenvalue Problems
item.description: arXiv:2601.08990v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the local convergence of nonlinear inverse iterations for eigenvalue problems arising from variational energies that are invariant under global phase rotations. This symmetry introduces an inherent degeneracy of the target eigenvalue, preventing the direct application of existing convergence results that require a simple eigenvalue. Within an abstract variational framework, we investigate a shifted Jacobian-based inverse iteration, known as the J-method, and establish its local convergence to quasi-isolated ground states. Our analysis shows that the target eigenvalue of the J-operator has algebraic and geometric multiplicity exactly two. By introducing an auxiliary iteration that fixes the global phase, we prove local linear convergence of the iterates modulo phase rotations and derive sharp convergence rates in terms of the spectrum of the J-operator. In particular, these rates can be improved through spectral shifting. We apply the abstract theory to a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation that models spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates, verify the relevant structural assumptions and numerically examine the quasi-isolation of the computed ground states. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the shifted J-method, particularly in regimes with slowly converging conventional inverse iterations.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Henning, Laura Huynh

item.title: Gradient-based collective and structured nonlinear dimension reduction with quadratic surrogates
item.description: arXiv:2602.01143v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is concerned with the approximation of continuously differentiable functions with high-dimensional input by a composition of two functions: a feature map that extracts few features from the input space, and a profile function that approximates the target function taking the features as its low-dimensional input. We focus on the construction of structured nonlinear feature maps, that extract features on separate groups of variables, using a recently introduced gradient-based method that leverages Poincar\'e inequalities on nonlinear manifolds. This method consists in minimizing a non-convex loss functional, which can be a challenging task, especially for small training samples. We first investigate a collective setting, in which we construct a feature map suitable to a parametrized family of high-dimensional functions. In this setting we introduce a new quadratic surrogate to the non-convex loss function and show an upper bound on the latter. We then investigate a grouped setting, in which we construct separate feature maps for separate groups of inputs, and we show that this setting is almost equivalent to multiple collective settings, one for each group of variables.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Pasco, Anthony Nouy

item.title: Taylor-Accelerated Neural Network Interpolation Operators on Irregular Grids: Higher-Order Approximation and Derivative-Informed Field Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2602.05589v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, a new class of Taylor-accelerated neural-network interpolation operators is introduced for quasi-uniform, irregularly distributed grids to reconstruct derivative-informed physical fields in both univariate and multivariate settings. The framework incorporates Taylor expansions within the neural network operators framework, allowing operators to efficiently utilize the smoothness of the target function. We determine the analytical properties of the proposed operators, including well-posedness, uniform boundedness, and exact interpolation at the sampling nodes. Additionally, we establish polynomial reproduction to a specified degree and provide Jackson-type error estimates based on higher-order moduli of smoothness, thereby improving convergence rates on quasi-uniform, irregular grids. The applicability of the method is demonstrated by reconstructing physical fields such as temperature, electromagnetic fields, and fluid properties, including pressure and velocity. The numerical results show that the proposed operators provide reliable, accurate estimates in the presence of noise and irregular sampling. The enhanced accuracy of the proposed method is validated by comparing it with current interpolation systems on irregular grids, including Lagrange-type methods.
item.dc:creator: Sachin Saini

item.title: Approximation of invariant measures for stochastic functional differential equations with infinite delay via an explicit finite-memory scheme
item.description: arXiv:2603.04724v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Owing to the intrinsic computational limitation that infinite memory cannot be stored numerically, the approximation of invariant probability measures (IPMs) for stochastic functional differential equations (SFDEs) with infinite delay remains an open problem. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing an explicit finite-memory truncated Euler-Maruyama scheme that combines memory and state truncation for such SFDEs. We establish strong convergence of the numerical segment process over any finite time horizon and obtain a convergence order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. We further prove that this numerical segment process admits a unique IPM and that its IPM converges to the exact counterpart under the $L^2$-Wasserstein metric as the step size vanishes, with an explicit convergence rate. The framework applies to both linear and superlinear coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Guozhen Li, Guoting Song, Shan Huang, Xiaoyue Li, Xuerong Mao

item.title: Residual Recombination Methods as Anderson-like Acceleration: An Algebraic Interpretation of BoostConv
item.description: arXiv:2603.20749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: BoostConv has been introduced in earlier works as an effective acceleration technique for nonlinear iterative processes and has been successfully employed in a variety of applications to enhance convergence rates or to compute unstable fixed points that are otherwise inaccessible through standard approaches. Despite its demonstrated practical effectiveness, the theoretical properties of the method have not yet been fully characterized. In this work, we present a more robust formulation of the BoostConv algorithm and, for the first time, provide a rigorous proof of its local convergence. The proposed analysis places BoostConv within a precise mathematical framework, clarifying its interpretation as a nonlinear convergence accelerator and establishing sufficient conditions under which convergence to a fixed point is guaranteed. The theoretical findings are illustrated through several numerical examples, spanning from a linear problem to a low-dimensional benchmark and a large-scale incompressible Navier-Stokes simulation. These results demonstrate the robustness and practical relevance of the proposed method and bridge the gap between empirical performance and rigorous analysis, paving the way for further developments and applications to complex nonlinear problems.
item.dc:creator: Vincenzo Citro, Davide Palitta

item.title: On Enhancing the Dissipative Behavior of Active Flux Advection Schemes
item.description: arXiv:2605.09669v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, the traditional third-order Active Flux advection scheme is modified by reformulating the method and introducing four additional parameters R, S, T, and U that allow the numerical dissipation and dispersion of the scheme to be adjusted. The influence of these parameters is studied using Fourier analysis and parameter choices that lead to schemes with improved dissipative properties are identified. These improvements are validated by numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Christian Klingenberg, Simon Krotsch, Philip Roe

item.title: A dual-field structure-preserving mixed finite element discretization for incompressible Hall MHD equations
item.description: arXiv:2605.19920v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-field structure-preserving mixed finite element discretization for the incompressible Hall magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations is introduced. It preserves pointwise mass conservation, magnetic Gauss law, and conservation of current density. It also satisfies a discrete energy law that exactly captures the correct energy dissipation rate in the dissipative regime and recovers energy conservation in the ideal limit. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the temporal and spatial accuracy and to illustrate the structure-preserving properties of the scheme.
item.dc:creator: Yi Zhang

item.title: Well-balanced second-order approximation of the compressible atmospheric Euler equations
item.description: arXiv:2606.19764v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a second-order approximation to the compressible atmospheric Euler equations with gravity that is invariant domain preserving and well-balanced with respect to stratified rest states, including isentropic and isothermal equilibria. The approximation is built upon discrete auxiliary states derived from a hydrostatic reconstruction of the density and potential temperature. These auxiliary states, together with an affine shift of the numerical state, provide local bounds needed for maintaining well-balancing and invariant domain preserving properties of the method. The numerical method is then verified and validated with analytic solutions, well-balancing tests, and typical benchmark problems for atmospheric flows.
item.dc:creator: Crystal Farris, Matthias Maier, Eric J. Tovar

item.title: Korovkin type theorems for operators acting on functions of polynomial and exponential growth on $[0,\infty)$
item.description: arXiv:2606.27517v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish two Korovkin-type approximation theorems for sequences of positive linear operators acting on continuous functions on $[0,\infty)$. The first result shows that pointwise convergence on all polynomial test functions implies pointwise convergence for every function in the domain that is dominated by a polynomial. The second result provides an analogous criterion for functions of exponential growth, where the test functions are the exponentials $e^{\lambda x}$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$. The results are applied to several classical and modified positive linear operators, including Baskakov, Sz\'asz--Mirakjan, Phillips, Post--Widder, Gamma, and Durrmeyer-type operators. Further applications are given to operators associated with modified Bessel functions and hyperbolic functions. The approach provides a unified framework for deriving pointwise convergence on unbounded intervals from convergence on suitable test functions.
item.dc:creator: Ulrich Abel, Ana-Maria Acu, Margareta Heilmann, Ioan Rasa

item.title: A Direct Approach to Hermite Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2607.17998v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a family of polynomials satisfying the natural duality relations for Hermite interpolation, analogous to the classical Lagrange interpolation polynomials. They yield an explicit closed formula for the Hermite interpolant with arbitrary multiplicities, without recourse to divided differences, recursive corrections, or auxiliary B\'ezout identities. We also give a detailed account of Hermite's original approach to the problem, based on an integral formula, which he used both to derive the interpolating polynomial and to estimate the interpolation error for holomorphic data.(To appear in L'Enseignement Math\'ematique.)
item.dc:creator: Simon Bossoney, Marc Troyanov

item.title: Domain-decomposed Evolutional Deep Neural Network with Random Features for Transient Pressure Diffusion with Discontinuous and High-Contrast Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2609.22349v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Transient pressure diffusion in heterogeneous porous media becomes difficult to resolve efficiently when permeability is discontinuous and spans several orders of magnitude. In this paper, we develop a domain-decomposed random-feature evolutional deep neural network (DD RF-EDNN) that separates spatial approximation from temporal evolution. Permeability-informed random features are compressed into an orthonormal pressure space, and a conservative finite-volume operator is projected onto this space so that only the reduced coordinates are advanced in time. This formulation retains the dissipative structure of the discrete flow problem without repeated neural-network optimization. The analysis quantifies dictionary and singular-value truncation errors, proves contractivity under an energy-consistent dissipativity correction, and derives a conditional grid-level estimate for homogeneous dynamics and time-independent data admitting a steady lifting. Numerical experiments on low-permeability inclusions, high-conductivity blocks and channels, and three-dimensional grids assess the accuracy of the method across distinct coefficient configurations. The method reaches a final-time relative $L^2$ error of $9.54\times10^{-4}$ in the principal benchmark and maintains errors on the order of $10^{-2}$ at a permeability contrast of $10^3$. Numerical diagnostics further show that the observed error balance and temporal convergence are consistent with the analysis. These results support DD RF-EDNN as a structure-preserving and interpretable reduced formulation for transient simulations on prescribed heterogeneous media.
item.dc:creator: Peiqi Li, Jie Chen, Hui Zhang, Simon Hands

item.title: A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain
item.description: arXiv:2610.19435v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.
item.dc:creator: Xinran Bai, Yu Du, Haijun Wu

item.title: Trace Inverse Estimates and Kernel-based Meshfree Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Interface Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27537v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kernel Galerkin methods allow meshfree trial spaces to be generated independently in each material subdomain and refined through their center sets, without generating an approximation mesh. We establish trace inverse estimates for products of Sobolev-kernel spaces on Lipschitz subdomains and use them to analyze symmetric Nitsche discretizations of linear elliptic interface problems. The estimates control gradient traces on subdomain boundaries by subdomain gradients, the interface jump, and an exterior boundary trace. Their conormal form supplies the flux control required for stability directly from the kernel and center assumptions, without a separate discrete flux hypothesis. For quasi-uniform center families with comparable fill distances and a fixed kernel scale, we obtain well-posedness for sufficiently large penalty parameters independent of refinement. We prove energy and $L^2$ error bounds of orders $h^{s-1}$ and $h^s$ for piecewise $H^s$ solutions, $2\le s\le m$, where $h$ is the maximum subdomain fill distance and $m$ is the kernel Sobolev order. The $L^2$ bound additionally requires piecewise $H^2$ regularity of the homogeneous adjoint interface problem. For kernels $\Phi_m(\varepsilon\,\cdot)$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$, we derive a scale-explicit condition-number bound in the kernel-translate basis and an $O(h^{-2})$ bound in an $L^2$-orthonormal basis. The analysis assumes exact geometry and integration. Planar experiments examine convergence and kernel scaling, while a three-dimensional heat-conduction problem in a curved composite illustrates the method.
item.dc:creator: Leevan Ling, Shu Ma, Weifeng Qiu, Yizhong Sun

item.title: Residual-based Adaptive Refinement of hp-Variational PINNs for elliptic PDEs with geometric singularities and localized features
item.description: arXiv:2610.37670v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks approximate the solution of boundary value problems by minimizing the strong-form residual, their accuracy is often limited near corner and crack singularities, sharp layers and localized features and the enforcement of Neumann boundary conditions remains challenging. In hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks, the problem is formulated in a Petrov-Galerkin weak form, reducing the differentiation order applied to the neural network, while boundary constraints are imposed through penalty terms. The variational residual is evaluated using fixed Gauss quadrature points and the strong-form residual on a fixed collocation set, which may fail to capture regions of rapid variation. To address this issue, we integrate hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Residual-based Adaptive Refinement. During training, the strong-form residual is computed on a dense candidate pool and points with the largest residuals are added adaptively to the collocation set. Since the weak formulation is defined in $H^{1}(\Omega)$, it avoids the $H^{2}(\Omega)$ regularity requirement that fails on cracked and non-convex domains. The proposed method is validated on four two-dimensional elliptic problems and consistently achieves substantial reductions in relative $L^{2}$, absolute $L^{\infty}$ and relative $H^{1}$ semi-norm errors through adaptive residual-driven point placement.
item.dc:creator: Somnath Giri, Muslim Malik, Rishikesh Yadav

item.title: Randomized algorithms in numerical linear algebra for scientific computing
item.description: arXiv:2610.38157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Randomized numerical linear algebra (RNLA) has fundamentally changed the landscape of scientific computing over the last twenty to thirty years. While early breakthroughs focused primarily on low-rank approximation and least-squares problems, randomized techniques are now used to solve a broad range of linear algebra problems, supporting applications spanning data science, optimization, and computational engineering. This paper surveys some of the main ideas of RNLA, focusing on methods that are effective in practice and on simple theoretical bounds that can be used to understand them. We highlight the core benefits of randomization: improved scalability, algorithmic simplicity, and---contrary to what the name may suggest---remarkable reliability and numerical stability. Topics include sketching, low-rank approximation, least squares, orthogonalization and approximate orthogonalization, randomized Krylov subspace methods, preconditioning, trace and spectral density estimation, row and column selection algorithms, posterior error estimation, randomized regularization, and tensor-structured randomness.
item.dc:creator: Ethan N. W. Epperly, Daniel Kressner, Yuji Nakatsukasa

item.title: A SPIDER-type stochastic subgradient method for expectation-constrained nonconvex nonsmooth optimization
item.description: arXiv:2501.19214v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many real-world problems, such as those with fairness constraints, involve complex expectation constraints and large datasets, necessitating the design of efficient stochastic methods to solve them. Most existing research focuses on cases with no {constraint} or easy-to-project constraints or deterministic constraints. In this paper, we consider nonconvex nonsmooth stochastic optimization problems with expectation constraints, for which we build a novel exact penalty model. We first show the relationship between the penalty model and the original problem. Then on solving the penalty problem, we present a single-loop SPIDER-type stochastic subgradient method, which utilizes the subgradients of both the objective and constraint functions, as well as the constraint function value at each iteration. Under certain regularity conditions (weaker than Slater-type constraint qualification or strong feasibility assumed in existing works), we establish an iteration complexity result of $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ to reach a near-$\epsilon$ stationary point of the penalized problem in expectation, matching the lower bound for such tasks. Building on the exact penalization, an $(\epsilon,\epsilon)$-KKT point of the original problem is obtained. For a few scenarios, our complexity of either the {objective} sample subgradient or the constraint sample function values can be lower than the state-of-the-art results by a factor of $\epsilon^{-2}$. Moreover, on solving two fairness-constrained problems and a multi-class Neyman-Pearson classification problem, our method is significantly (up to 466 times) faster than the state-of-the-art algorithms, including switching subgradient method and inexact proximal point methods.
item.dc:creator: Wei Liu, Yangyang Xu

item.title: DRO: A Python Library for Distributionally Robust Optimization in Machine Learning
item.description: arXiv:2505.23565v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce dro, an open-source Python library for distributionally robust optimization (DRO) for regression and classification problems. The library implements 15 DRO formulations and 9 backbone models, enabling 85 distinct DRO methods. Furthermore, dro is compatible with both scikit-learn and PyTorch through a unified interface, and uses approximation techniques to reduce runtime for some computationally demanding formulations. Comprehensive documentation is available at https://python-dro.org.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Wang, Jiashuo Liu, Henry Lam, Hongseok Namkoong, Jose Blanchet

item.title: Derivation of the fourth-order DLSS equation with nonlinear mobility via chemical reactions
item.description: arXiv:2510.07149v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a derivation of the one-dimensional fourth-order DLSS equation based on an interpretation as a chemical reaction network. We consider the rate equation on the discretized circle for a process in which pairs of particles occupying the same site simultaneously jump to the two neighboring sites; the reverse process involves pairs of particles at adjacent sites simultaneously jumping back to the site located between them. Depending on the rates, in the vanishing-mesh-size limit we obtain either the classical DLSS equation or a variant with nonlinear mobility of power type. Via EDP convergence, we identify the limiting gradient structure to be driven by entropy with respect to a generalization of diffusive transport with nonlinear mobility. Interestingly, the DLSS equation with power-type mobility shares qualitative similarities with the fast diffusion and porous medium equation, since we find traveling wave solutions with algebraic tails or compactly supported polynomials, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Mielke, Andr\'e Schlichting, Artur Stephan

item.title: Neural network approximation of regularized density functionals
item.description: arXiv:2511.18512v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study neural-network approximation of density functionals in a Banach-space setting. Since the exact continuum functionals are discontinuous in the natural density topology, we apply $p$-Moreau-Yosida regularization. We construct finite-rank ReLU networks that preserve convexity and nonnegativity, lie below the regularized functional, and approximate it uniformly on compact sets. For energies obtained by minimization over compact density sets, we account exactly for the energy shift caused by regularization and bound the remaining error by the localization on these compact sets and network approximation errors. We apply this framework to canonical and grand-canonical density-functional theory at fixed particle number and fixed mean particle number, respectively. We obtain uniform energy convergence on norm-compact classes of external potentials, including molecular Coulomb potentials. We illustrate our results through numerical experiments on a simple model system.
item.dc:creator: Andre Laestadius, Mathias Oster

item.title: Inference-Time Alignment for Diffusion Models via Variationally Stable Doob's Matching
item.description: arXiv:2601.06514v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inference-time alignment for diffusion models aims to adapt a pre-trained reference diffusion model toward a target distribution without retraining the reference score network, thereby preserving the generative capacity of the reference model while enforcing desired properties at inference time. A central mechanism for achieving such alignment is guidance, which modifies the sampling dynamics through an additional drift term. In this work, we introduce variationally stable Doob's matching, a novel framework for provable guidance estimation grounded in Doob's $h$-transform. Our approach formulates guidance as the gradient of the logarithm of an underlying Doob's $h$-function and employs gradient-regularized regression to simultaneously estimate both the $h$-function and its gradient, resulting in a consistent estimator of the guidance. Theoretically, we establish non-asymptotic convergence rates for the estimated guidance. Moreover, we analyze the resulting controllable diffusion processes and prove non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for the generated distributions in the Wasserstein-2 distance. Finally, we show that variationally stable guidance estimators are adaptive to unknown low dimensionality, effectively mitigating the curse of dimensionality under low-dimensional linear subspace assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method and show the advantages compared to the baselines.
item.dc:creator: Jinyuan Chang, Chenguang Duan, Yuling Jiao, Ruoxuan Li, Yi Xu, Jerry Zhijian Yang

item.title: A Thin Sheet Volume Integral Equation Solver for Simulation of Bianisotropic Metasurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.21474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A thin-sheet (TS) volume integral equation (VIE) formulation incorporating generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) is presented for the simulation of three-dimensional (3D) bianisotropic metasurfaces. The metasurface is represented as an equivalent thin sheet, with its constitutive tensors derived from the GSTC susceptibility tensors. Invoking the thin-sheet approximation, the governing VIEs are reduced to surface integral equations (SIEs), in which tangential and normal flux density components are treated as distinct sets of unknowns and discretized using Rao-Wilton-Glisson and pulse basis functions, respectively. In contrast to conventional GSTC approaches based on conventional SIEs, which represent only tangential fields, the proposed framework rigorously enforces the bianisotropic GSTCs, including normal field interactions, while retaining the flux-based VIE character of the formulation. Numerical examples, including a comparison with an SIE-GSTC solver that neglects the normal susceptibility components, demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed TS-VIE-GSTC solver for polarization rotation on planar and curved sheets, perfect reflection, beam steering with spatially varying susceptibilities, multi-directional attenuation, and oblique phase-shift transformation.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Celis Sierra, Meruyert Khamitova, Ran Zhao, Sadeed Bin Sayed, Hakan Bagci

item.title: Continuum-marginal optimal transport: a mesh-free kernel method
item.description: arXiv:2604.24226v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we study continuum-marginal optimal transport. Given a time-continuous family of probability marginals, the problem is to recover the minimum-energy velocity field whose flow reproduces every marginal. This problem is the continuum limit of the classical two-marginal Benamou-Brenier formulation, and also the deterministic limit of the Nelson problem of stochastic optimal transport. We propose a practical mesh-free solver for this problem. The weak continuity equation is embedded in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, yielding a sample-only objective that requires no spatial discretization. The velocity is parametrized by any linear-in-parameters dictionary or neural network, and is optimized by mini-batch stochastic methods. Synthetic experiments confirm that the method achieves accurate drift recovery and marginal consistency. The same computational framework also applies to the Nelson problem.
item.dc:creator: Yumiharu Nakano

item.title: Derivative Computation in PINNs: Automatic Differentiation, Finite Differences and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2608.11020v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We systematically investigate finite-difference (FD) derivative computation in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) as an alternative to automatic differentiation (AD). On three benchmark PDEs we show that, with a properly calibrated step size, FD matches AD in accuracy on every problem while running faster across the full tested batch-size range and using substantially less GPU memory, and that a stochastic variant we propose outperforms AD on a stationary problem. We further show that for neural architectures with inter-sample dependencies (e.g. BatchNorm, self-attention) the standard PyTorch autograd idiom is silently incorrect; the correct per-sample alternative is computationally infeasible at PINN-relevant batch sizes, while FD provides a forward-only approximation that is empirically an order of magnitude closer to the true per-sample derivative.
item.dc:creator: Maciej J. Mikulski, Tadeusz Uhl

item.title: Adaptive Schauder Stochastic Mirror Descent in Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.13121v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we solve risk functional minimization problems with general losses in Banach spaces within the framework of stochastic approximation. We introduce an adaptive regularization strategy for stochastic mirror descent (SMD). Specifically, using a Schauder basis, we construct nested finite-dimensional subspaces whose dimensions adapt to the sample size $n$ to balance approximation and optimization errors. We solve each SMD subproblem over the corresponding subspace and project the stochastic subgradient onto its dual space. This yields closed-form solutions and coordinate-wise coefficient updates with low computational and storage complexity. For risk minimization in $\mathcal{L}^p$ spaces with $1<p<\infty$, we construct Bregman distances adapted to the uniform convexity of the underlying Banach space using $\max\{2,p\}$-convex functionals. At the $\mathcal{L}^1$ endpoint, we instead construct a locally strongly convex functional based on the entropy function. By developing a new analytical framework, we show that the risk functional values converge to the minimum at a rate of $\mathcal{O}\left(n^{-\min\{\frac12,\frac1p\}}\right)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the misspecified setting, we prove convergence under weaker regularity assumptions and derive explicit polynomial rates under suitable regularity conditions. Finally, we apply the method to statistical inverse problems and illustrate its empirical performance through numerical experiments in both settings.
item.dc:creator: Jinhui Bai, Shuai Lu, Lei Shi

item.title: Optimal Condition Numbers in Low-Rank Positive Semidefinite Matrix Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2608.22418v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we focus on the stability of positive semidefinite matrix sensing maps $\Phi_{\mathcal{A}}=(\langle A_i,X\rangle)_{i=1}^m$ where $A_i\succeq 0$, $X\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r$. We introduce the bi-Lipschitz constants of $\Phi_{\mathcal{A}}$ and define the global condition numbers as the ratio of upper and lower Lipschitz constants. We give deterministic universal lower bounds for these condition numbers that depend only on the rank $r$ and on the underlying field. We then show that rank-one Gaussian measurements asymptotically attain these bounds, except for the operator-norm condition number over $\mathbb R$ when $r=1$. For this exceptional case, we establish a sharper universal lower bound and prove its asymptotic sharpness. As an application, we derive stability guarantees for an $\ell_1$-residual PhaseLift-type estimator at the optimal sampling scale. These results identify the intrinsic limits of conditioning in positive semidefinite matrix sensing and connect these limits to stable low-rank recovery.
item.dc:creator: Mingxuan Sun, Zhiqiang Xu

item.title: Characteristic Mapping Method for Vlasov-Poisson with BGK-collisions
item.description: arXiv:2609.16328v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work presents the first steps for simulating kinetic plasmas with collisions using the characteristic mapping method (CMM). The CMM is a semi-Lagrangian method that uses the group structure of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms to efficiently represent the flow-maps of transport problems. Individual submaps can be composed to follow the flow backward in time to its initial foot point, numerically establishing the back-to-label symmetry. The novelty of the presented work is the handling of the source term by storing the Duhamel integrals of each time sub-interval, allowing efficient temporal-integration. Furthermore, we use the Lagrangian structure to avoid implicit time-stepping in the hydrodynamic regime, which is known to be stiff. We benchmark our method on the Boltzmann-BGK and Vlasov-Poisson-BGK equations and consider different test cases, the Sod shock tube problem and nonlinear Landau damping for different Knudsen numbers. We show third-order spatial and temporal convergence and illustrate the fine-scale zoom property of CMM for the bump-on-tail instability.
item.dc:creator: Xi-Yuan Yin, Philipp Krah, Zetao Lin, Jean-Christophe Nave, Kai Schneider
